cleared.check: Upcoming fork, Karst on Celo and X Layer (planned for Celo in the fourth quarter of 2026 without a date, not present in the X Layer chain spec): what changes for the PoolManager and for funds inside it when a transaction is capped at 16,777,216 gas, CLZ becomes an opcode, MODEXP and P256VERIFY are repriced and predeploys are replaced by the L2 Contract Manager.
cleared.result: No loss or freeze path for an ordinary account. Liquidity removal has no loop: Pool.modifyLiquidity updates two ticks, flips at most two bitmap bits and clears at most two ticks (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-204), so its gas does not depend on what other accounts did. A swap loops over initialized ticks (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437) and stops at the caller's price limit, so a swap that would exceed the cap can be sent in parts. A stranger who fills ticks with dust raises the cost of crossing them and cannot stop an exit. The PoolManager makes no fixed gas call: take, the token transfer and the hook call forward all gas (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). CLZ occupies an opcode that the build for Cancun does not emit. The replaced predeploys can change which special addresses accept value or answer token calls, which is left as a lead.

cleared.check: Upcoming fork, Lagoon (in development, no date, announced for OP Mainnet and Unichain first): can the post execution transaction or the settlement of sequencer defined metering raise or lower a balance of the PoolManager outside a transfer (A2).
cleared.result: No. The settlement credits the sender of each refunded transaction and debits the block beneficiary, the base fee vault and the operator fee vault. The PoolManager cannot be the sender of a transaction, because it has no private signer and EIP-7702 delegation applies to accounts with a signer, and it is none of the three debited accounts. The post execution transaction itself charges no fee and moves no balance. Both chains' clients contain the plumbing, and neither chain has announced Lagoon.

cleared.check: Upcoming fork on Ethereum, Glamsterdam (not scheduled for mainnet, earliest mid January 2027 according to the 19 November core developer call, held up by EIP-8037 and EIP-8038): does the L1 fork change execution on Celo or X Layer for the PoolManager.
cleared.result: No. The fork changes Ethereum execution and headers. The X Layer op-node release xlayer/v0.1.7 supports the new L1 header fields, and Celo moved to celo-reth because op-geth will not support the L1 fork. L2 gas rules stay at the OP Stack fork of each chain. A third party survey of 11 October 2026 found a tracking issue for Amsterdam on the OP Stack without a schedule (https://nonceworks.com/notes/glamsterdam-gas-changes-operators.html). Two side effects are operational. Nodes on op-geth cannot follow after the L1 fork, and forno still answers part of its requests from an op-geth build. The cost of an L1 deposit used as forced exit changes with L1 gas rules. The mid January estimate comes from a press report of 21 November 2026 (https://cryptoslate.com/ethereums-glamsterdam-delay-reveals-a-troubling-pattern-behind-its-biggest-network-upgrades/).

cleared.check: Proposed change on Celo, migration to the second custom gas token design of the OP Stack: would the new predeploys NativeAssetLiquidity and LiquidityController, or the changed value rules of the other predeploys, give an ordinary account a way to move the PoolManager's native balance or to be credited for value it did not pay.
cleared.result: Not from the published specification. NativeAssetLiquidity accepts calls from LiquidityController only. LiquidityController.mint is limited to minters that the owner of the L1 ProxyAdmin authorises, and burn needs a caller that sends its own value. A mint to the PoolManager address by an authorised minter would raise the native balance without a settle, which is a governance action. The value sink at L2ToL1MessagePasser that F-047 lists for Celo would close, as it is closed on X Layer. Celo has not published its migration, so the fate of the CELO token proxy and of the transfer precompile under that design is an open lead.

cleared.check: Leads L-187 and L-216, second part: has any deposit source hash been written to the X Layer blacklist contract, and which accounts are operators.
cleared.result: None at block 76,668,710. The contract's storage trie has four leaves, which are the implementation slot, the admin slot, the owner and the initialized flag, verified from the storage root up to the state root of the block. A listed hash or an appointed operator would each add a leaf. The finding F-046 describes a capability that has not left a trace in state. An entry added and removed again inside the 85 percent of the log range that cycle 3 could not read would not show in storage.

cleared.check: Does the X Layer gasless whitelist give zero priced transactions to the PoolManager or its periphery, which would let an ordinary account run the dust tick filling of F-038 or other spam against pools at no cost.
cleared.result: No for the selectors tested. getGaslessAllowance returns false for the PoolManager, the PositionManager, both Universal Routers and Wrapped OKB with the selectors of unlock, execute, modifyLiquidities, transfer, settle, sync and deposit and with empty calldata. It returns true with 200,000 gas for a USDT0 transfer, which lets any account send USDT0 to any address for free, the PoolManager included. Such a transfer outside a sync and settle pair credits nobody (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) and stays in the PoolManager as surplus. The whitelist has many more entries, which I did not enumerate.

cleared.check: Known weakness of the Celo client before Karst: the refund counter of a fee currency transaction can go negative and wrap, which gives the sender the maximum gas refund. Can it move a balance of the PoolManager or be used against a pool.
cleared.result: No. The wrap changes how much of the debited fee the sender of that transaction gets back through creditGasFees, at the expense of the fee recipients. The amounts are minted and burned on the sender, the block beneficiary and the fee handler. A pooled fee currency held by the PoolManager is not touched, and the main branch clamps the counter from Karst on.

cleared.check: Part one. Full list of pool currencies from the whole Initialize history of the PoolManager on Base, BNB Smart Chain, World Chain and X Layer (leads L-396, L-317, L-291, L-353).
cleared.result: All four lists are complete from the deployment block. Base: 15,540,638 pools and 15,315,529 distinct currencies from blocks 25,350,000 to 61,262,999, read through base.gateway.tenderly.co in 35,913 windows of 1,000 blocks with no failed window. 14,831,656 currencies sit in exactly one pool. Twelve random windows were read again through base.rpc.sentio.xyz and gave the same log counts, and the totals of the two ranges that cycle 5 read in full agree to within the boundary windows. BNB Smart Chain: 341,903 pools and 78,255 currencies from blocks 45,970,610 to 135,285,510, the cycle 5 rows from the NodeReal endpoint plus 870 new ones. That endpoint stopped answering during this run with the message that the public usage limit is reached, and later reads used bsc.api.pocket.network. World Chain: 4,760 pools and 826 currencies from blocks 9,111,872 to 38,053,882 through the QuickNode endpoint. cleared.check: Single token bonding curve hooks with flags beforeInitialize, beforeAddLiquidity, beforeSwap, beforeSwapReturnDelta that hold native ETH, BNB or AVAX (SatoHook 0x0000f07d2b5f1ddf3244b8780f972f306efd2888 with 981.27 ETH, SurtHook, Sat1Hook, VitaHook, SatopegHook on Ethereum, BloomHook, HookTemplate, J3sseHook on Base, three SatoHook copies and AizoHook on BNB Smart Chain, one on Avalanche, NakamotoHook with 25.89 ETH on Robinhood Chain): they accept a second pool. Can it reach the reserve?
cleared.result: No. SatoHook source lines 224 to 231: beforeInitialize requires currency0 native, currency1 the hook's own token, fee 3000 and this hook, so a second pool can differ in tick spacing only. beforeSwap (253 to 272) checks the two currencies again and trades against one curve state (ethCum, totalMintedFair), so every pool of the hook is the same market for the same token. beforeAddLiquidity always reverts. The probe confirms it for the family: foreign pairs revert with InvalidPool and only the own pair with another tick spacing is accepted. For the hooks other than SatoHook I relied on the probe and on the matching error selectors, without reading each source.

cleared.check: RobinVistaHook 0xc2988a37d611779ad34b561231ee33603d15a0cc on Ethereum (160 pools, claims of 9.24 ETH plus PEPE, UNI, ONDO and others, about 18,100 USD) keeps accrued and banked fees per launch token, and poolIdOf[launchToken] is overwritten on every registerPool. Can an account register a second pool of a token with another base currency and withdraw in it? LongHook 0xfb6369c30573f9af1b88314c732fca944a34e0cc on Arc has the same mappings.
cleared.result: Not through the deployed factory. The ledger has the Klik shape: fees are added to accrued[launchToken] in the base token of the swapping pool and withdrawn in the base token of the pool that poolIdOf[launchToken] points at (hook lines 178 to 199, 296 to 366). registerPool and beforeInitialize accept allowed factories only, and one FactorySet log exists, for RobinVistaFactory 0x5407f136d0ddd6e6edcf5d2720ee7e26eeb9ac9a. Its launchToken (lines 309 to 419) deploys a new clone token for every launch and takes the base token from an owner curated registry, so each launch token has one pool and one base token. The fault would open if the owner allowed a factory that registers a pool for an existing token. For LongHook I read the mappings and the factory gate only, and did not read its factory.

cleared.result: OndexHook stores treasury, creator, holder and liquidity amounts in ledger[PoolId] (lines 100 to 108) and accepts initialize from its factory only (258 to 263). LaunchHook stores launches per pool id, its FeeEscrow is claimable[recipient][currency], and beforeInitialize requires the hook itself as sender. LaunchpadHook stores curves per pool id and creatorEthOwed per coin, all 211 pools pair with native ETH, and beforeInitialize requires a curve already registered for the pool id. EthCreatorFeeHookV3 stores its configuration per pool id and accepts the registrar of that configuration only. None of them pays from a ledger that omits both the pool id and the currency.

cleared.check: TurbineHook 0x1be2e33d8f468c09c1aa9e53d54e400470b2a088 (three pools, claims of 14,720 USDC and 0.4 WETH): beforeInitialize registers any currency pair with tick spacing 1 from any caller, and beforeSwap mints input claims and burns output claims. Can a pool opened by a stranger burn the claims of the real pools?
cleared.result: No. beforeSwap, mint and burn carry the routerOnly modifier (lines 222 to 280 and 370 to 424), so only swaps sent by the Turbine router reach the claim moves, with the output amount supplied by that router. The hook keeps reserve0 and reserve1 per pool id and updates them with checked arithmetic, and a source comment at line 246 states that the ERC-6909 balance cannot be used because it aggregates all pools of the hook. A new pool starts with zero reserves, so a swap out of it reverts on the subtraction. The router itself was not read.

cleared.check: Launch pad hooks named in L-395 that have verified source: CashCatHook and CashCatHookV2, PonsV2MemeHook, the proxy 0x4eb1976978756bd56802d8162f2271844924e0cc and FablesRamp on Robinhood Chain, MinaraFeeHook, WonkHook and LaunchHook on Arc, TaxLaunchHook on X Layer and Base. Is the ledger that decides a payout stored under the pool id, a token or a currency, and who may initialize?
cleared.result: All are stored under the pool id or under the currency that is paid. CashCatHookV2: pending and tab per pool id, platformTab per currency, initialize from the factory only and currency0 must equal the configured quote (line 273). CashCatHook: per pool id, native quote only. PonsV2MemeHook: pendingFees, pendingCreatorTax and pendingBuyback per pool id and currency, factory only. 0x4eb19769 is an ERC-1967 proxy of LunchTaxHookPair: accruedQuote per pool id, owed per recipient and quote token, launcher only. FablesRamp: range ledgers per pool, distributorOwed and claimFeeOwed per currency, initialize needs a fee cap configured for the pool id. MinaraFeeHook: creatorAccrued per pool id, platformAccrued per currency, launcher only with an allowed quote. WonkHook: per pool id and currency, initialize needs a registered launch. TaxLaunchHook: configuration and fee slots per pool id, escrow per recipient and currency, factory only. The factories were not read, so whether a launcher may choose the quote currency is answered only where the hook checks it (CashCatHookV2, MinaraFeeHook). ZoraV4CoinHook 0x0469a4bd3724dc86c9542f4694c976da13c450c0 on Base holds nothing in the currencies checked and rejects initialize.

For a foreign pool beforeSwap reverts with 0x3b99b53d (0x87fa6e44 on the unverified one) because the swap carries no signed quote, and afterSwap alone reverts with Panic(0x12). The claim withdrawal function was not read.

cleared.check: PolHook 0xa33c9bcd5cada0636f19350d7461003c38814088 and 0xb721b4f9771ed66f85c0ffbf9504f1eaab154088 on Polygon have the same shape as the Arbitrum route hooks: beforeSwap takes the PoolKey input currency and trades hardcoded DAI and USDT on a Curve pool from the hook balance (source lines 53 to 115). They hold 3.0 DAI each and 2.24 USDT. Can a foreign pool empty them?
cleared.result: Not today. In the Quoter test inside an unlock the hook takes the foreign currency and Curve pulls 2.9994 DAI from the hook, and then exchange_underlying reverts because the Aave V2 lending pool 0x8dff5e27ea6b7ac08ebfdf9eb090f32ee9a30fcf rejects the deposit with error string "3". The same revert hits the hooks' own DAI and USDT pool, so the hooks are out of service. The balances are about 3 USD each. beforeSwap in this source has no caller check either. If the Aave reserve accepts deposits again the path opens.

cleared.check: Hooks that call PoolManager.take or PoolManager.swap with hardcoded currencies inside beforeSwap for any pool, and hold nothing: Unichain proxy 0xad78e0a3b5a552813feb5eb8ecbe842f7b5e9088 (takes native ETH and swaps on a real pool for a foreign PoolKey) and the exact output branch of CamelotHook on Arbitrum One. Can this move PoolManager funds to the swapper?
cleared.result: No. take debits the hook in the currency it names (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and the delta it returns is credited in the currencies of the foreign PoolKey (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:299-311), so the hook is left with a debt in the real currency that nobody settles and unlock reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The Quoter shows a result only because it reverts before that check. A loss needs a hook that owns claims or balances, as in the two findings.

cleared.check: Unverified hook 0x6bc99d37114ae54b782c7694368ed5430e9c0ac8 on Arbitrum One (1001 USDC and 1001 USDT on the hook, two pools, no initialize flag): afterSwap does not look at the PoolKey. For any pool it reads prices from 0x451d7e6f and calls PositionManager.modifyLiquiditiesWithoutUnlock on its own position 0x2afe.
cleared.result: No loss shown. In the Quoter test for five foreign PoolKeys the third modifyLiquiditiesWithoutUnlock call reverts and afterSwap fails with a wrapped error, so a foreign pool cannot be swapped at all. The rebalance uses the oracle price and the hook's own position, and anyone can trigger the same code by swapping in the real pool. Whether a foreign swap can succeed in another state and move the position at a price the attacker sets was not established and is listed as a lead.

cleared.check: Step 1. Which pooled tokens with a market price are worth more than 1,000 USD at each PoolManager today. Method: currency lists of cycle 4, live balanceOf(PoolManager), prices from coins.llama.fi (cycle 5 price files for 18 networks; this cycle priced every currency with a balance on Robinhood Chain, Elysium and Arc, 738,773, 129,491 and 261,204 addresses).

Zora and HyperEVM have no priced token above the threshold (2 and 11 priced currencies, all below 1,000 USD). The lists are complete where cycle 4 read every Initialize log (Ethereum, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Arc and the other networks with an init census). They are incomplete on Base, BNB Smart Chain and X Layer, where the cycle 4 list holds only currencies that moved in its window, and on World Chain, where it comes from an explorer page. A census of Base Initialize logs started in this cycle counted 2,418,681 currencies in the first 10,000,000 blocks after deployment against 9,116 on the list, and was stopped for size. Two values are price artefacts and were kept as targets: PORT3 on Ethereum and vUSDT on BNB Smart Chain, whose balanceOf returns more than one word. Token lists with values are in the discover files.

cleared.check: Step 2. For each of the 2151 tokens: every selector of the token, of its implementation and of the contracts that balanceOf(PoolManager) touches (eth_createAccessList, 1442 related contracts) was called from an ordinary account with the PoolManager as address argument. Named functions got arguments by type; the 14775 selectors without a known name got eight fixed calldata shapes. Each trial ran in eth_call with a measuring stub at the PoolManager address and was repeated with the block time moved by 8 hours, 91 days and 400 days. Mode A: the stub hands one third of the balance to the account first. Mode B: the PoolManager sends nothing and the account holds a balance written by state override into the token's balance slot. Mode C: as B without a balance, for tokens whose slot was not found. Measured: balanceOf(PoolManager) before and after, the account's balance, and whether a transfer of the full balance leaves the PoolManager.
cleared.result: Mode A 2318914 trials, 140312 calls accepted by the token. Mode B 2279949 trials on 2019 tokens, 133089 accepted. Mode C 38965 trials on 132 tokens. Batches that failed for lack of gas were rerun with eight trials per call and none is left open. One priced token ended a trial with a higher reported balance and a refused full transfer: QANX 0xaaa7a10a8ee237ea61e8ac46c50a8db8bcc1baaa on Ethereum through transferLocked, at every block time. That is finding F-078 and nothing new (21,210,277.64 units at the PoolManager, 205,708 USD at the coins.llama.fi figure that F-078 already calls unreliable). No trial lowered balanceOf(PoolManager) of a priced token, at any of the four times. Every other accepted call that raised the balance took the same amount from the caller and left the full balance transferable (transfer, transferAndCall, multiTransfer, batchTransfer, transferShares and equals), or differed by one or two base units of share rounding. The full list of functions through which a caller's tokens reached the PoolManager is transfer, transferFrom, transferAndCall, transferWithMemo, multiTransfer, batchTransfer, push, move, transferShares, bridgeTransfer, bridgeTransferFrom, transferMultiple, transferForMultiAddresses, transferWithReference, transferFromWithReference, multisend and bulkTransfer. None is a grant, a lock or a deposit for another account, so no priced token offers the grant and revoke sequence of F-079, and no selector without a name raised the balance. One mode B result is an artefact: claimRewardsAndStake on stkAAVE paid the account's own rewards, which exist only because of the overridden balance, to the PoolManager. Control: DeadToken on Base (F-085) is not detected in mode A, because the hand-out by the PoolManager resets its idle timer, and is detected in mode B at 91 and 400 days (claimIdleTokens lowers the balance to 0 and the account gains half). Limits: the trials measure the token's own balance only, so a public call that pays a second asset to the PoolManager is not seen; arguments such as Merkle proofs and signatures are not satisfied; on Monad no endpoint accepted a block override, so Monad was tested at the current time only.

cleared.check: Does the passage of time alone change the PoolManager balance of a target token or stop it from sending the full balance (expiry, demurrage, cooldown, scheduled rebase)? One block was pinned per network and the trial without any call was run at 0, 8 hours, 91 days and 400 days, with and without a hand-out.
cleared.result: Six tokens change, all Aave receipt tokens whose balance grows with interest: aEthLINK, aEthWETH, aEthUSDC and aEthUSDT on Ethereum, aArbUSDT on Arbitrum One and aBasWETH on Base (each between 1,500 and 5,800 USD). No token lost balance with time and no full balance transfer turned from accepted to refused at any of the shifted times. Monad could not be tested for lack of a block override.

cleared.check: Precompile tokens have no selector table in code: 35 B20 tokens on Base (OUSD with 5.3 million USD, the tokenized stocks with suffix c, cbZEC, cbHYPE) and the 5 TIP-20 tokens on Tempo. The function lists were taken from the published interfaces and run through the same trials.
cleared.result: Base B20: 30 state changing functions of IB20, IB20Asset and IERC8056; 3,920 trials per mode; an ordinary account gets transfer, transferWithMemo and approve accepted and nothing else. mint, burnBlocked, seizeWithMemo, pause, updatePolicy and the multiplier setters need roles, and the interface states that balanceOf stays in raw units while the multiplier scales the UI view only. Tempo TIP-20: 29 functions, 620 trials per mode, the accepted calls are transfers, approve and calls that act on the caller. burnBlocked and burnAt need roles, and rewards are claimed by the holder for itself. Issuer powers over these tokens are in F-027 and the Tempo findings of earlier cycles.

cleared.check: Lead L-399, FOLD 0xe172e9b6cfbeeb5593bdce3f077356fdb33af904 (24,275,769 FOLD at the PoolManager, about 742,000 USD). A transfer from CLAIM_SOURCE locks the amount at the recipient until NO_MORE_LOCKS. Can any account still cause such a transfer to the PoolManager, and can the owner name a later claim source?
cleared.result: No. setClaimSource reverts once a source is set (InterfoldToken.sol lines 416 to 422) and CLAIM_SOURCE() returns the auction 0x687cc38d8279df3352b64cf3ec1fe8e033933595. The auction pays tokens to the bid owner only (claimTokens and claimTokensBatch) and accepts bids only while it is active. All 310 bids were read at Ethereum block 26,478,229: none has the PoolManager as owner, 10 are not exited and 1 is exited with 8.33 FOLD unclaimed, all owned by other addresses. lockCount(PoolManager), queuedLockCount(PoolManager) and lockedBalanceOf(PoolManager) are 0 and transferableBalanceOf equals balanceOf. The remaining ways to place a lock (linkClaim, mintAllocations) need LOCK_MANAGER_ROLE or MINTER_ROLE, and minting is closed since tge. Locks end for everyone at NO_MORE_LOCKS = 1915884000 (17 September 2030).

cleared.check: Step 3, tokens where balanceOf counts units that transfer cannot move (apart from QANX): who can create such units at another address? Sources read: ondo, skl, SPA, WLFI, SIERRA, fxSAVE and its base pool.
cleared.result: Only role holders or the holder itself. ondo: transfers are limited to the freed balance when investorBalances is set; the trial call of the setter by an ordinary account reverted. skl: SkaleToken refuses a transfer that would leave less than the locked amount, and the three lockers add to it through TokenLaunchManager (role), through the holder's own delegation and through a slash of the holder's delegation. SPA: transferWithLock is onlyOwner. WLFI: the transfer hook blocks legacy users that are not activated, a registry state set by the owner; staking locks sit in a separate contract. SIERRA (LYTPool) and the fxUSD base pool lock shares of an open redeem request, and a request is made by msg.sender for its own shares. The PoolManager has made none of these calls and cannot make them (its calls to a currency are transfer and balanceOf, src/types/Currency.sol:60-95).

cleared.check: Step 3, staking and vault tokens with cooldown, vesting or escrow words: sUSDe, sENA, sPENDLE, apyUSD, aptUSD, syrupUSDC, syrupUSDT, syrupUSDG, yUSD, yETH, svZCHF, SiloVault shares (USDC on Arbitrum One, mevUSDC on Avalanche by selector match), Yearn vaults on Base.

The vesting in sUSDe, sENA, yUSD, yETH, apyUSD and aptUSD is the release schedule of vault yield and touches no holder balance. redistributeLockedAmount needs the admin role and a restricted source address. Maple pool shares are a plain mapping and every transfer passes a permission check of the pool's manager contract. The remaining risk is the issuer side (deny lists, pause), which earlier findings hold.

cleared.check: Step 3, tokens with lock or escrow functions that act on the caller, and one that locks for a named recipient: AST, BNB, RNDR, TITANX, HEX, DPR.
cleared.result: AST lockBalance, BNB freeze, RNDR holdInEscrow and the TITANX and HEX claim, stake and mint functions act on msg.sender. The TITANX burn functions for another user spend that user's allowance. DPR transferWithLock(to, reason, amount, time) moves the caller's tokens into the token contract and records a lock for the recipient. The locked amount is outside balanceOf(recipient). unlock(of) can be called by anyone after expiry and pays the amount to the recipient, so it is a public call that raises the PoolManager balance with the locker's own tokens, which is the class of F-041 without a gain.

cleared.check: Step 3, launch pad tokens with lockPool, vesting, allocation or cap data: the DERC20 family on Base (33 tokens above 10,000 USD of one selector set, 4.2 million USD together), CloneDERC20VotesV2, Zora CreatorCoin and ContentCoin, DopplerERC20V1 on Robinhood Chain (10 tokens), StonkCoin (STONKFI, 1.18 million USD), SEND LaunchToken, GANG.
cleared.result: Vested amounts are held by the token contract and paid on release to the beneficiary, so they are outside balanceOf of holders. lockPool blocks transfers to one pool address and is onlyOwner; pool() was read for all 44 tokens above 10,000 USD with these functions and none names the PoolManager. DopplerERC20V1 adds a holding cap for receivers while isBalanceLimitActive, which reads 0 on the Robinhood Chain tokens read. StonkCoin.balanceOf adds claimableAllocation(account), which the first transfer turns into balance. The allocation comes from the account's own backing of the raise before launch (StonkFi.back uses msg.sender), claimableAllocation(PoolManager) is 0 and the raise is launched, so no account can create one for the PoolManager. SEND pays holder rewards in a second asset to msg.sender on claim. These tokens are made by the launch pads, and what their owners can do is pool-creator scope.

cleared.check: Step 3, tokens whose matching functions are freeze, seize, reclaim or rescue functions: PYUSD, PAXG, USD1, EURI, FDUSD, U, UUSD, cbBTC, AUSD, frxUSD, WPRL, XGZ, geod, ESPORTS, USDSC, mUSD, rsETH, weETH, USUALX, LBTC, BTC.b, WBTC, wTAO, BBTC, eure, LCX, SWFTC.
cleared.result: In the sources read these functions carry a role or owner check (modifier or an explicit sender test), and no trial call of them by an ordinary account was accepted. PAXG has a rewards module since its last upgrade: an account joins a payout group through the registrar role, through its own EIP-712 or ERC-1271 signature, or by accepting a proposal itself. The PoolManager has no isValidSignature and cannot accept. Rewards are paid from the claim source to the group's destination and leave the account's balance unchanged. This group is issuer scope and is covered by the issuer findings (F-019, F-036 and the Ethereum issuer finding of cycle 5).

cleared.check: Step 3, reward, claim and reflection tokens: ENS and 00 (Merkle claims), PNK, LDO, NMR, DBR, JEFE, MONTRA on Elysium, stkAAVE, G$, FWA and RIP, and the tokens without verified source (gAIX and KTI, MONTRA implementation, PAXG implementation on Base).

JEFE is a reflection token whose balance at every holder rises with taxed transfers, a known class without gain for the sender. MONTRA pays rewards in KNTQ and reports isExcluded(PoolManager) = 1 and earned(PoolManager) = 0. FWA and RIP allow transfers to and from the PoolManager only inside a hook granted allowance, which is a design of the pool author. G$ is covered by F-056 and an earlier cleared item. cleared.check: OpenZeppelin audit, C-01: an ERC-20 representation of the native currency lets one payment be credited twice, once as msg.value under address(0) and once as a balance increase under the token, which drains native pools (worked case Celo, with Polygon as a network where deltas can be inflated).
cleared.result: Closed in the source. Hazard in one sentence: sync the token face, pay with settle and value, then settle the face for the same inflow. Closing statements: a settle with value reverts while any token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356); a native credit is taken from msg.value only when no currency is synced (353-354); every write of a nonzero synced currency also writes the reserves (285-286, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so a face synced after a native payment starts from the higher balance; a token settle clears the slot (361); the contract has no receive or fallback function and only settle and settleFor are payable (300-307). The report says the fix makes the next settle after a sync settle that currency or revert. The source is looser in one way: sync(address(0)) clears the slot without a settle (283, documented at src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:165-171). I walked the orders that this allows and each inflow is still credited under one id only, because the stale reserves are overwritten by the next token sync. Reliance: A1 (the synced currency lives in transient storage for one transaction and is rolled back on revert), A2 and A3 (native value reaches the PoolManager through settle, and anything forced in is credited once under one id). Per network: an address that reports the PoolManager's native balance exists on Celo (CELO token, transfer works), Arc (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000, six decimals, transfer works), Polygon (0x1010, transfer of 1 without value returned false), Optimism and Zora (LegacyERC20ETH, transfer disabled). My query found no such answer from these candidates on the other 16 networks, and the ledger holds a face search for each of them. On all 21 deployed PoolManagers my walk with a stub token that returns the native balance of its argument gave: sync while locked succeeded, settle with 1000 wei reverted with NonzeroNativeValue, a zero value settle paid 0 and cleared the slot, settle with 1000 wei then credited 1000, a new sync and settle of the face paid 0, and a native take of 1000 closed the unlock. The real faces on Celo, Polygon, Arc, Optimism and Zora gave the same seven answers. The walk shows the contracts deployed today. The checkout was not compiled.
cleared.source: docs/security/audits/OpenZeppelin_audit_core.pdf pages 10-11; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 300-307, 349-365; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32; eth_call with state overrides on the 21 rpc URLs of state/networks.json on 2026-11-23 (scripts walk.py and faces.py, results raw/walk.json and raw/faces.json in cycles/007/core-code-audit-walk-a.work); cleared items of core-code-accounting (cycle 1), core-code-invariants-settlement (cycle 2) and core-code-loose-guards (cycle 6)

What src provides is separation: pool state is stored per pool id (src/PoolManager.sol:93), deltas per caller and currency (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41), hook deltas are booked to the hook address in the two currencies of its pool (PoolManager.sol:181, 224, 381-384). The ledger records where these fail per network (rebasing and reward tokens F-012, F-041, F-066, F-067, F-091, tokens that move or burn the PoolManager balance F-085, F-086, F-090, F-099, issuer controls F-057, F-080). cleared.check: OpenZeppelin audit, M-01: assembly blocks marked memory-safe wrote past the scratch space or over the free memory pointer (hook return data, the TickMisaligned error, two argument custom errors, the ERC-20 transfer call).
cleared.result: Closed. The hook return data is copied to memory at the free memory pointer, which is then advanced by the padded length (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:140-149). TickMisaligned and the two argument revert helpers build their data at the free memory pointer and revert at once (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:57-63, src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:49-79, 83-118). The single argument helpers write 36 bytes into the 64 byte scratch space (CustomRevert.sol:14-46). The ERC-20 transfer writes its 68 bytes of calldata at the free memory pointer, reads the answer into the first scratch word and zeroes the three words it used (src/types/Currency.sol:55-80). Reliance: A10 only, that MSTORE, MLOAD, RETURNDATACOPY and CALL behave as on Ethereum, which cycle 1 tested on every network.

cleared.check: OpenZeppelin audit, L-03: fromId turns a uint256 into a currency and drops the upper 12 bytes, so mint and burn could act on an id that differs from the currency. The report says the team added a mask to fromId.
cleared.result: Closed. fromId casts the id to uint160 (src/types/Currency.sol:114-118), which drops the upper 96 bits, and mint and burn pass currency.toId() to the claim ledger and not the raw argument (src/PoolManager.sol:324-327, 333-335). A raw id with upper bits therefore debits or credits the same currency and the same claim id as the clean one, and no claim can exist under an id with upper bits, because _mint is reached only from line 327. The direct ERC-6909 functions take raw ids (src/ERC6909.sol:25-56) and find a zero balance under any id with upper bits. The closing statement uses no property of the chain, so it holds on all 21 networks alike.

cleared.check: Trail of Bits audit, settlement invariants UNI-SETTLE-1 to UNI-SETTLE-13: a settle never raises what the user is owed beyond the amount paid, the amount paid equals what reached the singleton, and burn, mint and clear move the delta and the claim balance by exactly the stated amount.
cleared.result: The source has these properties for a token whose balance changes only by transfers. settle credits msg.value or the checked balance difference and nothing else (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). burn adds the amount to the caller's delta and removes it from the claim balance of from after the operator or allowance check (332-336, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/ERC6909.sol:85-89). mint does the reverse (322-329). clear accepts only the exact positive delta and sets it to zero (310-319). Every amount passes toInt128, which rejects 2^127 and above (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59). Reliance: UNI-SETTLE-3 rests on A2 and A3. It fails by design for a token whose balanceOf rises without a transfer from the settler, and the ledger lists those per network (F-041, F-066, F-067, F-079, F-081, F-091).

cleared.check: Trail of Bits audit, take invariants UNI-TAKE-1 to UNI-TAKE-3: after a take the caller's delta falls by the amount, the recipient's balance rises by it and the singleton's balance falls by it.
cleared.result: UNI-TAKE-1 holds from the source alone: the debit is written before the transfer and the call reverts as a whole if the transfer fails (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-53, 81-86). UNI-TAKE-2 and UNI-TAKE-3 rest on A3 and A4 and the source cannot enforce them: the token branch accepts an empty answer or a 32 byte 1 and makes no code size check (Currency.sol:64-74), so a take of an address without code moves nothing, and a token may deliver less to the recipient or charge the sender more. In each case the caller is debited the full amount, so the shortfall falls on the caller, except where a token charges the PoolManager on top, which the ledger holds as F-092 for Ethereum, Arc and BNB Smart Chain. Unit theme-transfer-side-effects of this cycle searches for further tokens of that kind.

cleared.check: Spearbit 5.2.5 (low, no response recorded): bubbleUpAndRevertWith copies return data of any size and pads the copy with whatever the memory held.
cleared.result: Nothing in src bounds the copy (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:83-119), and callHook also copies the full return data of a successful hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:140-149). The wrapped revert runs only after a native transfer, token transfer or hook call has already failed (Currency.sol:51-53 and 82-86, Hooks.sol:137), so the transaction reverts either way, and a hook that returns very large data can only stop actions in its own pool. The padding bytes can expose stale memory in the revert data, which holds no secret, because the contract keeps none: all of its storage and transient storage is public through extsload and exttload (A11). Gas for memory growth is a chain property (A9, A10), and a higher price for it makes the same call fail earlier. No path treats the failed call as a success.

One synced currency and its balance are written together and the currency slot alone marks whether a sync is pending (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-38, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 350-362). A zero balance is stored as zero. The reliance is A1: transient storage must be private to the PoolManager, roll back with a reverted frame and be empty at the start of each transaction. The per network status of A1 is the one recorded in state/cleared.json by the transient storage units, and this unit ran no new chain query for it. It also relies on A2 and A3 for the meaning of the balance, as recorded for the native face networks in F-008, F-050 and the settlement models of earlier cycles.

cleared.result: Closed in both copies: src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-13 and src/libraries/TransientStateLibrary.sol:38-39. The only reliance is A10, the EVM semantics of the bit and arithmetic opcodes. The opcode vector probes recorded in state/cleared.json found these equal to Ethereum on all 21 networks, and this unit ran no new chain query for it.

The only reliance is A10, the EVM semantics of the bit and arithmetic opcodes. The opcode vector probes recorded in state/cleared.json found these equal to Ethereum on all 21 networks, and this unit ran no new chain query for it.

Monad: types 0, 1, 2 and 4 and the staking system transaction. MegaETH: legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-7702, deposit, mega system transaction, pre-block calls and the KeylessDeploy sandbox.

cleared.check: Inherited caller on MegaETH. From a frame that the PoolManager called, do the natively implemented behaviours (Oracle sendHint, KeylessDeploy, MegaAccessControl, MegaLimitControl) act on the PoolManager when reached by DELEGATECALL, CALLCODE or STATICCALL, and does a switch set by a callee outlive the callee?
cleared.result: No. The interceptors test the target address, which under DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE is the calling account, so those kinds run the contract's Solidity code and revert with NotIntercepted for MegaAccessControl and MegaLimitControl. KeylessDeploy reverts with NotIntercepted under every kind from an inner frame. CALL and STATICCALL of disableVolatileDataAccess take effect for the calling frame and its descendants, and after that frame returned the frame at the PoolManager address read isVolatileDataAccessDisabled false and a TIMESTAMP read succeeded. The effect stays inside the frame that asked for it, which is the hook and token case of F-018.

cleared.check: Lead L-324, second part: does a deposit that fails for lack of the 60,000 intrinsic gas count as one new state entry, and can the deposits of one L1 block fill the block budget of 1,000 entries?
cleared.result: It counts when the sender account is empty: the entry is recorded before the final gas test and the failed deposit path does not reset the limiter. The portal sells 20,000,000 gas per L1 block and requires at least 21,000 per deposit, so at most 952 such deposits fit, and a deposit of 1,000,000 gas can write about 41 new slots, so twenty of them add about 840 with their sender accounts. Both are below 1,000, and deposits run first in their block.

cleared.check: Inherited caller, HYPE bridge: a contract called by the PoolManager with value uses DELEGATECALL into the code at 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222. The log then reads Received(PoolManager, payout amount) although no HYPE reached the bridge. Does HyperCore credit the PoolManager's account, or anyone, for it?
cleared.result: No. The log is emitted by the calling contract and HyperCore credits only logs emitted by the bridge address. Chain history holds a controlled case: on 2026-10-22 a contract emitted Received with the bridge layout for a user and 0.0001 HYPE without paying the bridge, 226 seconds after the same user's real payment of the same amount. HyperCore credited the real payment and nothing else within an hour. Thirteen other logs of this layout from other emitters also have no credit. If the node honoured such logs, any contract could forge them with LOG2 and no PoolManager would be needed.

cleared.check: Exits, tick crossing cost. Can an ordinary account place dust positions so that another user's swap can never be included under the gas cap, or so that a liquidity removal fails.
cleared.result: It can raise the cost of a swap and cannot block it. Each loop pass ends at the nearer of the next initialized tick and the caller's price limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-420), so a swap that would cross more ticks than fit under 16,777,216 gas is done in several transactions with a price limit each. A crossing reads the tick and writes two fee growth words (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612), which by the gas schedule is at most about 50,000 gas when both words are written for the first time, so one transaction still crosses several hundred initialized ticks. The party that initializes a tick pays more gas for it than a swapper pays to cross it. modifyLiquidity touches the two ticks of the position and no others (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), so dust on other ticks does not change the cost of a removal. On Unichain a full sweep is at 61 percent of the cap today, so added dust ticks would force a full sweep of that pool into two transactions.

cleared.check: Exits under a censoring or halted sequencer. Is the forced path through L1 deposits still open for a position owner after Karst and Azul, and can an ordinary account close it.

Deposits are exempt from the 16,777,216 gas cap and are limited to 20,000,000 gas per L1 block, and a block that omits them is invalid. On Base nodes derive the missing blocks themselves after a sequencing window of 3,600 L1 blocks. A removal through the deployed PositionManager needs a few hundred thousand gas. An account that fills the deposit gas market pays L1 fees for every block it fills. This matters only when the sequencer already censors, which needs the operator.

cleared.check: Lead L-484, part one: every code path of the B20 stablecoin and asset logic v3, the factory and the policy registry at v1.5.6 that writes a balance or an allowance, and who may call it.
cleared.result: Balances are written in move_balance, burn_inner and mint. move_balance is reached from transfer with the caller as source, from transferFrom after the allowance of the source for the caller is checked, and from seizeWithMemo after the Seize role check. burn_inner needs the Burn role on the caller's own balance or the BurnBlocked role on a blocked account. mint needs the Mint role. Allowances are written by approve for the caller and by permit for the recovered signer, which must equal the owner. The asset variant adds batchMint (Mint role) and announce, which needs the operator role and then routes its inner calls with the same caller and the same privilege flag. The privilege flag that skips policy and role checks is true only inside the factory's creation of a token, and the factory builds the token object from the address it has just computed and checked to hold no code, so the flag cannot reach an existing token. The credited account is the named recipient: the recipient strategy returns the given address or an error for zero and for the token itself. A caller without a role can therefore change another holder's balance only by paying into it.

cleared.check: Known weakness: the Base block production halts of 25 and 26 June 2026, caused by journal state kept after a rejected transaction. Could an ordinary account use that fault, or one like it, to carry the unlock flag, a delta or a synced currency of the PoolManager into another transaction (assumption A1).
cleared.result: No funds path. The state that leaked was the warm set of a transaction that failed validation, before any code ran, so it held no transient writes of the PoolManager. A block built on a contaminated journal is rejected by every node that executes it from a clean journal, which is what halted the chain, so a leaked value cannot become canonical state. The fault let whoever sent the rejected transaction stop block production for about two hours, which delays exits and takes nothing. At v1.5.6 catch_error calls discard_tx for every error that is not a failed deposit, and a failed deposit reverts to the first checkpoint and commits.

cleared.check: Known weakness: op-reth and kona accepted deposit transactions written as a bare RLP body without the 0x7E type byte (fixed by optimism pull request 22778, released in op-reth v2.4.3). Could an ordinary account use it to run a call with a sender or a value that nobody authorised.
cleared.result: No for an ordinary account. The pull request describes a bypass of the leading-byte gates of derivation, which read batches. Batches are written by the batcher of the chain, so the party that could have placed an unsigned deposit, with a chosen sender and a mint, is the operator. Unichain, Ink and Soneium report op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1, which is later than v2.4.3. Zora reports conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, which is later by number only, since the Conduit build has its own numbering. The page lists four referencing pull requests numbered 4970 to 4973 with the title fix(consensus): reject non-canonical transaction encodings and does not name their repository, so the state of the Base client is not confirmed. I did not confirm the fix in the build of the OP Mainnet sequencer, which reports no version, or in the op-reth revision that World Chain v2.8.2 pins, and I did not read the decoder itself.

cleared.result: None could. The high findings are an abort of execution on oversized pairing input and a changed access order in a frozen logic version, both consensus faults and both fixed. Storage writes of native precompiles skipped the 2,300 gas stipend check of EIP-2200. The PoolManager forwards all gas on every call it makes (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and holds no guard that relies on the stipend, so this changes nothing for it. Value sent to nonpayable factory and activation registry selectors was stranded and is now rejected, which the sweep of this cycle confirms. permit accepted high-s signatures, which still need the owner's own signature. Calls to B20 shaped addresses without a token revert before any token logic, which the auditors and the sweep both state. Unknown block list ids authorize every account and unknown allow list ids authorize none, and updatePolicy refuses an id that does not exist. The remaining items concern gas metering, refunds, metrics, string storage and test coverage.

None gives an account on L2 a way to change a PoolManager balance, a delta or a claim. The 200 ms block review has three low findings about stale lookups after a reorg and proof history.

One caller, three ids over one balance (address(0) in wei, the token face 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 in units of 10^12 wei, the USDC implementation address 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6), sync before and inside the unlock, settle, take, mint, burn, payment through the face, native value forced in by SELFDESTRUCT, a payout to the PoolManager itself, and collectProtocolFees through the fee adapter that any account can call.
cleared.result: No order gains more than one face unit minus one wei per settle, which is less than 0.000001 USDC. On chain at block 32,767,874: (a) 752,591,764,406 wei forced in after sync of the face raised the reading by one unit and settle credited 1 unit, a gain of 247,408,235,594 wei; (b) with the balance on a unit boundary, a native take of 1 wei lowered the face reading by one whole unit, and after a new sync 1 wei forced in was credited as 1 unit; (c) collect of the face through the adapter while the face is synced reverted with ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced, collect of 1 wei of native fees was allowed (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49 exempts address(0)) and lowered the face reading by one unit, after which settle reverted with a panic on the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360; (d) with the implementation address synced, collect of the face was allowed and settle panicked the same way; (e) take of the face with the PoolManager as recipient left the balance unchanged, settle credited 0 and the caller kept the debit; (f) a native take to the PoolManager and any take under the implementation id reverted, also for amount 0. Fee collection therefore only lowers a reading inside a bracket. It gives the caller a free way to place the balance just below a unit boundary, where earlier models needed a native debit of 1 wei. A bounded search over a model with the unit scaled to 4 base units (4,062,481 states at depth 10, fee collection and forced value included) found a best gain of 3 base units with one settle and 6 with two, that is one unit minus one base unit per settle. Each such settle needs a value-bearing call for the forced wei, which costs at least 9,000 gas, 1.8 * 10^14 wei at the 20 gwei fee floor, against a gain below 10^12 wei. Pool operations and hook deltas move amounts inside one currency id and add no cross id move, so they were left out of the model.

cleared.check: Critic gap of cycle 6: the code of the Arc fee adapter and of the jar it pays. Can an ordinary account choose the recipient of a fee collection, receive the fees, or re-enter the PoolManager through the payout while it is unlocked.
cleared.result: No. collect has no caller check and passes the immutable TOKEN_JAR as recipient, so the caller chooses only currency and amount. The jar has an empty receive function, so the native payout of src/types/Currency.sol:48 runs no code that calls back. The jar pays out only through release, which requires the releaser, a WormholeReleaser contract under the same governance path as the PoolManager owner. triggerFeeUpdate lets any account push the fee that the pool override or the policy gives, and src/ProtocolFees.sol:37 caps it at 1000 pips per direction. cleared.check: L-284 as far as it can be answered before the fork: what do the ConfigurableAccount precompile and an account with the 0xef marker answer to the call shapes of take, sync, unlock and the hooks once T14 rules apply.
cleared.result: The node already contains the T14 code and applies it when a simulated block carries a time after 1796742000. Under that time all 15 shapes from the PoolManager address to 0xAACC000000000000000000000000000000000000 revert, so the address stops acting like an account without code. An account with code 0xef and no registered configuration fails every shape with OpcodeNotFound before and after. For a registered account the source of the shim returns success with empty data for empty calldata, answers isValidSignature and onERC721Received, and reverts with empty data for every other selector, so it cannot serve as a currency, a hook or a direct caller of unlock. cleared.check: L-255: does any crate of the Tempo node at commit 697ea97 start a transaction inside a running user call through evm2 committed_copy, call_tx or transact, which would give the inner execution an empty transient map.
cleared.result: No. In 351 modules of 13 crates committed_copy and call_tx do not occur at all. transact is used by tests and by the payload builder's prewarming worker, which executes whole pool transactions on a separate EVM and detaches the result. The transaction handler changes the initial call depth around a batch and runs the batch calls on the same state and the same transient map. Precompiles have no way to call a contract, as cycle 3 recorded. The zone crates and the test and fuzz crates were not searched; zones are separate chains. The answer holds for this commit and has to be repeated for the next release that mainnet adopts.

cleared.check: L-197: what the v1.18.2 item EVM call input hardening and the v1.18.4 fix for EVM execution changed, and whether the PoolManager's call and return data sequences depend on it.
cleared.result: v1.18.2 introduced evm2 with a patch that passes call input as a borrowed range of the caller's memory. At the mainnet revision the range is resolved through the caller frame on each read, so growth of the child's memory cannot corrupt it, and output is written to the caller's memory after the child has ended. v1.18.4 added a check that the remaining gas covers the input cost before a precompile or the T14 account marker copies its input, in crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs and crates/evm/src/instructions.rs, and changed no other module of the seven execution crates I compared. The PoolManager's calls use disjoint input and output ranges for transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73), no output range for hooks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and Solidity's same range pattern for balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:94). A differential of 32 cases that cover these three patterns, a child that grows its memory and a second call after the memory was rewritten matched revm byte for byte. Cycle 4 established that the jit feature is absent from the default build and that 256 swaps and 288 adds through the deployed bytecode matched the source formulas. Not confirmed: which features each validator compiles in.

cleared.check: Calldata width as the deployed contracts enforce it. The pool id is the hash of the PoolKey struct as it sits in memory (src/types/PoolId.sol:11-15), and take, sync, mint and the claim getters use address and uint24 arguments as mapping indexes and call targets. No line of src rejects a word with bits above the declared width, so the question is whether such a word can reach the hash, a delta slot or a mapping and give one pool or one currency a second identity.
cleared.result: It cannot on any of the 21 deployed PoolManagers. I sent 47 eth_call requests to each of them. initialize with a clean struct returns tick 0. The same call reverts with no return data when bit 160 is set in the currency0 word, the currency1 word, the hooks word or the price word, when bit 24 is set in the fee word or the spacing word, and when the spacing word is 0xffffc4 without sign extension. The properly sign extended value -60 reaches the code and returns TickSpacingTooSmall(-60) (src/PoolManager.sol:120). protocolFeesAccrued, balanceOf, isOperator and sync revert with no data for an address word with a high bit set, and balanceOf accepts an id with bit 200 set and returns 0, because the id is a full uint256 there (src/ERC6909.sol:17). The 24,050 byte Unichain contract gave the same answers as the other 20. Nine endpoints report the empty revert with data 0x and twelve with no data field, which is a property of the RPC server. These are answers of the deployed contracts. For the build under review the same rejection comes from the ABI decoder that solc 0.8.26 generates, which I could not run here.

cleared.check: Address words that reach CALL without a mask. Three assembly lines pass an address to CALL as it stands: the recipient of a native payout (src/types/Currency.sol:48), the token of an ERC-20 payout (Currency.sol:73) and the hook (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). Earlier readings listed the masked uses only. Can a word with bits above 160 make the PoolManager call a different account than the one it books, on a network whose CALL treats such a word differently?
cleared.result: No. The three values come from ABI decoded arguments, which the first item shows are rejected when dirty, or from fromId, which truncates to 160 bits (src/types/Currency.sol:116-118). The debit is booked under the same value masked to 160 bits (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-13), so even a dirty word would name one account in both places as long as CALL uses the low 160 bits. I tested that on every network with one eth_call that has no to address and runs CALL, STATICCALL, EXTCODESIZE and BALANCE on a word with bits 160 and 200 to 231 set above the identity precompile address 0x04. On all 21 networks CALL and STATICCALL returned the 32 input bytes, which only 0x04 does, and BALANCE of the dirty zero address equalled BALANCE of address zero.

cleared.check: Slot index folding on every network. F-040 showed that Avalanche treats slot S and S with bit 248 flipped as one storage slot and compared only Polygon and BNB Smart Chain. Does any of the 21 networks fold another single bit of a storage slot index or of a transient slot index, which could let two PoolManager slots (the four transient constants, a delta slot, a pool, tick or position slot) share one cell?
cleared.result: Only Avalanche folds, only bit 248, and only for persistent storage. Test one: extsload(bytes32[]) on each deployed PoolManager for the 256 indexes that have exactly one bit set. Every word was zero except index 2 (the fee controller, where one is set) and, on Avalanche, index 2^248, which returned the owner stored in slot 0. Test two: one eth_call without a to address that stores 0xAA at storage slot 0 and 0xBB at transient slot 0 and then loads all 256 one-bit indexes of both kinds. Storage returned nonzero at bit 248 on Avalanche and nowhere else. Transient storage returned zero for all 256 indexes on all 21 networks. For the PoolManager on Avalanche the fold stays harmless: fields of one struct sit at S, S+1, S+2 and so on up to S+6 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:83-91, 68-77; src/libraries/Position.sol:19-25), and S xor (S+n) for n from 1 to 6 always has a set bit below bit 3, so it never equals 2^248. All other slots are keccak256 outputs, and the transient slots that carry the lock, the deltas and the synced currency are not folded anywhere. The probe sees a rule that drops one bit. It does not see a rule that needs two or more bits to change.

cleared.check: Storage addresses that coincide at run time for caller chosen input. The Solidity bug SOL-2026-7 (leads L-028, L-151, L-152) can only bite where two storage or memory addresses meet at run time. Which statements of src let a caller make two separately computed storage slots equal, and does the deployed code handle that case as the source says?
cleared.result: One place: ERC6909.transfer and transferFrom with receiver equal to sender, where balanceOf[sender][id] is lowered and balanceOf[receiver][id] is raised through two slot computations (src/ERC6909.sol:25-48). Every other pair is kept apart by a check or lives in transient storage, which the affected optimizer steps do not track according to the Solidity post: currency0 is below currency1 (src/PoolManager.sol:121), tickLower is below tickUpper (src/libraries/Pool.sol:95), struct fields use fixed offsets from a pointer that is assigned once, and the hook and caller deltas are transient (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41). I tested the one place with eth_simulateV1, which sends nothing: for a current holder of a claim, balanceOf, transfer of the whole balance to itself, balanceOf, transferFrom to itself, balanceOf, and a transfer of one unit more than the balance. On Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Unichain (the 24,050 byte contract), Ink, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium the balance was the same before and after both self transfers and the oversized transfer reverted with an arithmetic panic. A stale read of the receiver balance would have doubled it. The endpoints of Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM do not offer eth_simulateV1 and those of World Chain, Celo and X Layer refused it. On Base, Soneium, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain the log query for a holder was refused, and on Zora and Tempo I found no holder in the log window. Those 14 networks were not tested. This is a test of the deployed code on one path. It does not answer the three leads, which need a compiler.

cleared.check: Invariants of flash accounting and custody as this checkout writes them, restated for the opcode focus of this cycle: which instructions each settlement statement depends on, and whether any edge of those instructions can change a credit, a debit, the counter or the lock.
cleared.result: The invariants are the seven of cycle 2 (lock, closure, credits, debits, custody, one payment bracket, claims) and the four chain properties T1 to T4, and I found nothing in the current text that changes them. I read src/PoolManager.sol:96-114 and 279-384, src/libraries/Lock.sol:8-27, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-34, CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41, CurrencyReserves.sol:11-38, src/types/Currency.sol:40-118, src/ERC6909.sol:25-89, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-59 and src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-70. The settlement path uses few instructions. The delta slot is KECCAK256 of two masked 32 byte words at memory 0 (CurrencyDelta.sol:12-14). The four fixed slots are literals. TLOAD and TSTORE hold the flag, the counter, the deltas and the bracket. The counter moves by ADD and SUB of 1 (NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:21, 31). The delta update is a checked int256 addition (CurrencyDelta.sol:37), so the compiler adds signed comparisons. The credit is a checked subtraction of two balances (PoolManager.sol:360). Every amount passes the cast at SafeCast.sol:56-59, which is a GT style comparison against 2^127. The counter cannot pass below zero: _accountDelta returns on a zero delta (PoolManager.sol:369), it decrements only when next is zero, which means previous was -delta and nonzero, and it increments only when previous is zero (373-377). Every input delta is below 2^127 in size, so the int256 sum at CurrencyDelta.sol:37 would need more than 2^128 calls to overflow. clear compares an int128 with the int256 slot value and can only bring a positive slot to zero (PoolManager.sol:310-319). mint and burn use the masked id currency.toId() for the claim and the truncated currency for the delta, so both sides name the same currency (PoolManager.sol:322-336, Currency.sol:110-118). None of these depends on SAR, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD, MULMOD or BYTE. KECCAK256 over 64 bytes, TLOAD, TSTORE, ADD, SUB, AND and the comparisons are in the 185,529 vector battery that OPCODES.md reports clean on all 21 networks. The rollback behaviour of TSTORE inside the PoolManager's own frames is not covered by that battery and is tested in the next item.

cleared.check: T4 on the deployed PoolManager of each network: after an unlock that fails inside a caller's frame (callback REVERT, callback out of gas, callback INVALID, callback that returns with an open delta), are the lock flag, the nonzero delta counter, the caller's delta slot, the synced currency slot and the caller's ERC-6909 balance back to zero, so that the caller cannot go on to call take, mint or burn without the closure check. Also: does a nested unlock revert, does settle with value revert while an ERC-20 is synced, and does take outside unlock revert.
cleared.result: Yes on all 21 networks. A driver placed by code override at an address with no code calls the deployed PoolManager seven times with eth_call; nothing is deployed or sent. In each callback the driver first calls mint(driver, 1, 1), which opens a delta of -1 for currency id 1 and writes a claim. Read from inside the callback before the revert, the lock flag was 1, the counter 1 and the delta slot -1 on every network, so the writes happened. After each failed unlock the driver read all five values through exttload and balanceOf and got zero on every network, for REVERT, for out of gas at 300,000 gas, for INVALID and for a callback that returned with the delta open, which unlock rejected with CurrencyNotSettled (0x5212cba1, src/PoolManager.sol:112). A callback that minted and burned the same amount returned success and left all five values zero. A nested unlock from inside the callback reverted with AlreadyUnlocked (0x5090d6c6, src/PoolManager.sol:105). After sync(0x04) inside the callback the synced currency slot held 0x04, and settle with 1 wei reverted with NonzeroNativeValue (0xb0ec849e, src/PoolManager.sol:356). take(address(0), driver, 0) after all of this reverted with ManagerLocked (0x54e3ca0d, src/PoolManager.sol:96-99). This confirms that inner writes are undone when the outer frame fails and that the lock cannot be left open by a caught failure, on the code path that eth_call uses on each endpoint. Blocks: Ethereum 26484005; Optimism 159956182; Base 61603838; Unichain 64762782; Zora 54408652; Worldchain 38087752; Ink 62012731; Soneium 31188195; Celo 83610382; X Layer 76742107; Arbitrum One 527071731; Robinhood Chain 122108085; Elysium 10268249; Polygon 97870450; BNB Smart Chain 135435881; Avalanche 101243669; Monad 124963667; MegaETH 32714131; Arc 32880504; HyperEVM 52108363; Tempo 50566887. Tempo needed a gas cap of 40,000,000 because a new storage slot costs more there; the result is the same. Unichain runs its own predeploy bytecode and gave the same result.

cleared.check: T3 on the deployed PoolManager of each network: does msg.value sent with settle arrive in the PoolManager's balance by the same amount inside the same frame, and does a native take of the same amount restore the balance, so that the credit at src/PoolManager.sol:354 matches a real payment.
cleared.result: Yes on all 21 networks. Inside the callback the driver read BALANCE(PoolManager), called settle with 5 base units, read it again, took 5 base units back with take(address(0), driver, 5), read it a third time and reverted. The second reading was the first plus 5 and the third equal to the first on every network, from 0 on Tempo (the driver's balance came from the state override) to about 3.18 * 10^24 on Polygon. The counter was 1 after settle and 0 after take. The PoolManager therefore sees the value as payment in the same unit as SELFBALANCE and BALANCE report it, and the native payout at src/types/Currency.sol:48 moves the stated amount.

cleared.check: Monad compiles frequently used contracts to x86 code, and eth_call runs the interpreter, so the probe above did not run the compiled path. Do compiled TSTORE and TLOAD keep the same rollback as the interpreter.
cleared.result: Yes, by reading the client source on the main branch. The x86 emitter compiles TLOAD and TSTORE to calls of the runtime functions runtime::tload and runtime::tstore (emitter.hpp lines 492-501, dispatched from x86.cpp lines 250-254). The interpreter calls the same runtime::tstore (instruction_table.hpp lines 1357-1375). runtime::tstore exits with an error under a static call and otherwise calls host set_transient_storage, and tload calls get_transient_storage (storage.hpp lines 38-62). The host writes into the current account state of the versioned State object (state.cpp lines 326-329 and 409-413), which is the version stack that the cycle 3 reading found to be popped on a failed frame. Compiled and interpreted code therefore share one transient store and one rollback, and the probe result holds for both. The remaining gap is that I did not confirm that main equals the mainnet release v0.16.5; web3_clientVersion on rpc.monad.xyz returned Monad/unknown.

cleared.check: Bor puts two shared caches in front of the interpreter: a cache of KECCAK256 results for 64 byte inputs and a jump destination analysis cache shared by the BlockSTM V2 workers and the prefetcher. Every delta slot (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-14), every ERC-6909 balance and allowance slot and every mapping slot of the pools is a 64 byte KECCAK256 input. Can either cache return a wrong slot or a wrong jump answer for the PoolManager.
cleared.result: No, as read at tags v2.11.0, v2.11.1 and develop. opKeccak256 uses the cache only when the input is exactly 64 bytes, keys it by the whole 64 bytes copied into an array, and stores a common.Hash value, which Go copies, so the shared hasher buffer cannot alias a stored entry (instructions.go lines 259-290 at v2.11.1, evm.go line 179 for the type of hasherBuf). The cache is a sync.Map with a size cap, and a speculative execution that is later discarded can only leave entries that are true hashes, because the value is a pure function of the key (keccak_cache.go, bounded_cache.go). The jump destination cache is keyed by the code hash as in go-ethereum and stores the bitmap computed from that code (contract.go lines 82-112). A collision in either cache needs a KECCAK256 collision. I could not confirm which bor release the endpoint runs; polygon.drpc.org answers web3_clientVersion with Geth/v10.0.0/drpc. The 64 byte cache is present at all three revisions read.

cleared.check: Re-entry through the four places where the PoolManager hands control to outside code while settlement state is open: the unlock callback, hooks, the ERC-20 transfer and balanceOf of a currency, and the recipient of a native take. Does any of them run before the PoolManager has written the debit or after it has read a value it then trusts.
cleared.result: No ordering gap in the current text. take writes the debit before the transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). mint writes the debit before the claim (326-327) and burn writes the credit before the burn, and the burn reverts the whole call when the balance or allowance is short (334-335, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/ERC6909.sol:85-89). _settle reads the synced currency, rejects value for an ERC-20, reads the balance, resets the slot and then credits, and the only outside call in it is the balanceOf staticcall, which cannot write state (349-364, src/types/Currency.sol:90-96). sync makes the same staticcall and then writes both slots (279-288). Hooks run inside the pool functions and their deltas are booked after the hook returns (178-183, 221-226, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-160). A re-entering party shares the lock but not the caller's delta slots, which are keyed by msg.sender (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-16), and unlock returns only when every slot of every party is zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). The cycle 2 victim and two account searches cover the sequences; this item confirms that the text they model has not changed in the lines they cite.

cleared.check: Token faces, in one line as the cycle focus asks: the earlier attempt at this unit left a sweep of currency pairs whose PoolManager balances move together and an extended settlement model.
cleared.result: The sweep in the work directory (8,436 named addresses, 2,085 pairs) shows one to one pairs that both pay out (EURe on Ethereum and Polygon), which the model gives no gain (setting 1, 17,367 states), and scaled pairs on Celo that do not pay out; the model gains only for scaled or rate faces that both pay, and the sweep lists none; not followed further in this cycle.

cleared.check: Exits: can an ordinary account make another user's liquidity removal or claim redemption impossible to include on these networks through gas caps, storage prices or the cost of tick crossings.
cleared.result: No. Removal runs Pool.modifyLiquidity, which has no loop and touches two ticks, at most two bitmap words, one position and the pool liquidity (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236). Its gas does not grow with the number of initialized ticks or positions. Under the Polygon storage prices of PIP-88 (cold read 5460, cold write surcharge 2940) the dozen cold slots of a removal add an estimated 40,000 gas to the 85,099 to 130,613 gas that the repository snapshots record for a removal (snapshots/PoolManagerTest.json:10-15). The caps are 16,777,216 gas on BNB Smart Chain, 33,554,432 on Polygon and the block limit of 80,000,000 on Avalanche. burn and take have no loop either (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 331-336). The swap loop is the only part of core whose gas an outsider can raise, and that is filed as a finding of this cycle with effect degrade.

cleared.check: Exits: special recipients. Can an outsider make the native payout of another user's take revert, or does any of the three chains refuse value transfers from the PoolManager to particular recipients.
cleared.result: No. The recipient of a take is chosen by the caller, and the native payout forwards all gas (src/types/Currency.sol:48). The earlier sweeps list the addresses that refuse value (system contracts that revert on empty calldata, the Polygon token contract 0x1010, the deprecated C-Chain precompiles), and a user reaches them only by naming them. The BNB Smart Chain client skips the value transfer only when the caller of the frame is the system address (core/vm/evm.go lines 291 to 347 at tag v1.8.2), which the PoolManager never is. The hard coded address filter of BNB Smart Chain applies to the sender and recipient of the top level transaction only, as cycle 1 recorded.

cleared.check: Known weakness and by design behaviour: the StateReceiver installed by Uburu lets any account replay a failed state sync. Can an ordinary account use the replay paths to make 0x1001 or FxChild call the PoolManager or its owner contract with data of its choice.
cleared.result: No. A replay must match the stored hash of receiver and data, or a leaf under the historic Merkle root, so the caller chooses only the time (StateReceiver.sol lines 85 to 133). The call is onStateReceive(uint256,bytes), which the PoolManager does not implement: an eth_call from 0x1001 to the PoolManager with that selector reverts with empty data. FxChild forwards to processMessageFromRoot on a receiver named in the record, and the PoolManager owner 0x8a1b966ac46f42275860f905dbc75efbfdc12374 reverts unless the caller is FxChild and the sender is the Ethereum timelock 0x1a9c8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be35bc. Any Ethereum account can send a record through FxRoot, and FxRoot writes that account as the sender. Of the 25 failed records pending since Uburu, 23 are for FxChild, and none has the timelock as sender or the owner contract as receiver. The 67 historic leaves that have not been replayed were not enumerated and are a lead.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of Bor disclosed in 2026 that earlier cycles did not judge: the four issues of v2.5.9 (handshake panic, header panic, state sync pagination, truncated block number checks) and the BlockSTM items of v2.10.3.
cleared.result: None gives an ordinary account a lever on PoolManager funds. The two panics and the two BlockSTM items stop or slow nodes. The pagination gap made nodes reject each other's blocks. The block number issue let an authorised producer present a block number far above the parent's, which matters to contracts that read block.number. The PoolManager bytecode has no NUMBER, TIMESTAMP or BLOCKHASH opcode (assumption A10) and its accounting closes inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The v2.10.3 post states that execution results are unchanged by its fixes, and the serial and parallel processors must agree on every block.

cleared.result: The function is disabled. A call reverts with the string Disabled feature. A signature transfer debits the recovered signer, and no signature recovers to a contract address, so the PoolManager balance could not be the source even if the function were live. The mirror of the native balance at 0x1010 stays as finding F-008 describes.

cleared.check: Known weakness: the superinstruction interpreter of BNB Smart Chain v1.7.x let SSTORE run inside a STATICCALL frame (pull request 3582). Does any accounting step of the PoolManager rely on the write protection of STATICCALL.
cleared.result: No. The PoolManager makes one kind of static call, balanceOf on a currency, in sync and in _settle (src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:285 and 359). A token that could write or re-enter during that call would gain nothing over calling the PoolManager before or after it: sync stores the currency and the returned balance after the call (src/PoolManager.sol:285-286), and _settle reads the stored reserves before the call, credits only the currency it read at line 350 and then clears the slot (lines 358-364). In both places the returned number is already chosen by the token. A token that is not written by the attacker does not re-enter. The pull request describes the outcome as wrong gas use and a bad block on nodes that ran the optimized interpreter, which was an opt-in flag. The changelog records that v1.8.0-alpha removed the interpreter, and v1.8.2 is mandatory before 2026-12-08.

cleared.check: The fork boundary of Jenner on 2026-12-08. Until then a transfer call to 0x70 or to a CAS20 address succeeds with empty data. Can an account create a debt, a credit, a claim or pool liquidity in such a currency before the fork that becomes a claim on real tokens after it.
cleared.result: No. Before the fork take of such a currency succeeds and only debits the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). A positive delta in it can come only from settle, which needs sync, and sync reverts because balanceOf returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94). mint adds a debt of the same size as the claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329). Pool operations move deltas between the caller, the hook and the pool and add to zero, so no unlock can close while any party owes the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Nothing denominated in the currency can therefore exist in storage when the fork arrives, except pools with zero liquidity. After the fork an uncreated CAS20 address reverts on every call, as cycle 5 saw on Chapel, and a created token is an issuer matter (F-007, F-076).

cleared.check: Lead L-331: do PIT, ASS, CATE and GFH charge the PoolManager more than the amount when it transfers them.
cleared.result: No. Eight simulated transfers per token set (one thousandth and one third of the balance, to a fresh address and to 0xdead) at block 135,335,118 all returned a 32 byte true. For ASS, PIT and CATE the PoolManager balance fell by slightly less than the amount, because the fee is taken from what the recipient receives and part of it is reflected to holders, the PoolManager among them. For GFH it fell by exactly the amount. take debits the caller the requested amount (src/PoolManager.sol:294), so a payout leaves the PoolManager whole or a few thousand base units ahead.

cleared.result: No. settle credits the rise of the PoolManager balance since sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). A transfer of one third of the PoolManager's PIT balance (168,336,790 PIT) paid a fee of about 6,733,000 PIT and raised the PoolManager balance by 0.0113 PIT. For ASS the same test paid about 1,604,000 ASS and raised it by 0.0026 ASS. The caller pays the whole fee and can be credited only the PoolManager's share of it, which is about two parts in a billion. Reflection that accrued before the sync is already inside the stored reserves and is credited to nobody.
