cleared.check: Open question of the cycle 6 and cycle 7 critics: does the C-Chain accept set code transactions, so that an account can carry a delegation and act as a hook or as a caller with code.
cleared.result: No. The code that decides block validity under Continuous Execution validates each transaction with an accept mask of legacy, access list and dynamic fee types (worstcase/state.go lines 181 to 193) and rejects a sender that holds code (lines 202 to 209). The CLZ opcode of Osaka is undefined on the public endpoint, which matches a rule set without the later Ethereum forks. Code at a hook address on the C-Chain can therefore change only through a contract's own upgrade path, as on Ethereum before EIP-7702 (assumption A7, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:337-339).

cleared.check: By design behaviour of Continuous Execution: consensus accepts a block before it is executed, includes a transaction when the sender can pay its worst case cost, and treats an execution error as fatal. Does any of this break the atomic settlement that unlock relies on, or let state reach the PoolManager outside a transaction.
cleared.result: No. Execution still applies transactions one by one with core.ApplyTransaction, in block order, each on the state left by the one before (saexec/execution.go lines 346 to 364), and cycle 2 showed that each call resets transient storage. A transaction that reverts is still included and charged, and all PoolManager state it wrote is rolled back with it. The fatal branch concerns a transaction that is invalid at execution time, which the worst case check exists to exclude. It would stop the chain for everyone and gives no account PoolManager funds. Whether an ordinary account can reach that branch is filed as a low lead.

cleared.check: Can a cross-chain import write into the storage of the PoolManager account. The C-Chain keeps balances of other X-Chain assets inside the storage trie of the holder.
cleared.result: No. At tip an import whose inputs or outputs carry an asset other than AVAX is rejected (cchain/tx/import.go lines 112 to 129). Asset balances live under slot indexes with the lowest bit of the first byte set, and contract code can only reach slot indexes with that bit cleared (cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go lines 45 to 62 and 124 to 171). An AVAX import raises the native balance, which cycle 2 cleared.

cleared.check: Transaction types and execution contexts of Ethereum against unlock, sync, settle and take: types 0x0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x3 and 0x4, the system calls at block boundaries, withdrawals, and bundles inside one transaction. Who is msg.sender, what is msg.value and what does transient storage hold in each?
cleared.result: Types 0x0, 0x1 and 0x2 differ in fee fields and access list only. Type 0x3 adds blob hashes that the PoolManager never reads and must name a recipient. Type 0x4 sets delegation designators before execution and then runs one ordinary top level call. In all five the sender is the signer, value is debited from the signer before the first frame, and the transaction has one transient map that is empty at the start. A delegated account can be the sender of unlock itself, and the walk with a designator placed by state override passed all four steps with tx.origin equal to msg.sender. A delegation that was set by a transaction which later reverted stays set, which changes code at an account and nothing inside the PoolManager. System calls use the system address as caller, a fixed target and their own transient map, and withdrawals credit balances without execution, as cycles 2 and 3 read in the specification. The census of 120 blocks found no sixth type. The remaining cross user effect is a sync left by an earlier call of the same transaction (F-071).

cleared.check: Critic gap of cycle 7: which Ethereum fork is scheduled, and does it add a transaction type with more than one frame? If the frame transaction of EIP-8141 were live, what would unlock, sync, settle and take see?
cleared.result: Glamsterdam is next and has no mainnet date; its scheduled EIPs add no transaction type. EIP-8141 is scheduled for the fork after it and has no activation date on any network. Read against the draft text: frames are top level calls that run one after another, and transient storage is discarded between frames, so each frame meets a locked PoolManager with no synced currency, and the stale sync of F-071 cannot cross a frame. unlock opens and closes inside one frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Value enters only in SENDER frames, where it is debited from tx.sender as in a CALL. In DEFAULT frames msg.sender is 0xaa for every author, value is zero, and the only functions that act for 0xaa without an unlock are sync, initialize and the ERC-6909 transfer and approval functions. 0xaa is not a valid hook address, because it sets the after add liquidity returns delta bit without the after add liquidity bit (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:113-116), so updateDynamicLPFee cannot be reached with it. The draft may change before it ships, and I did not read a client implementation.

cleared.check: The Hoodi activation of Glamsterdam was withdrawn because EIP-8037 breaks assumptions of deployed contracts. Does the source hold such an assumption: a fixed gas amount for a call, a gas check, or a path that must fit a gas figure?
cleared.result: No. The three external call sites forward gas() (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), the unlock callback and balanceOf are plain high level calls, and a search of src outside src/test finds no gasleft and no numeric gas argument. Under the current text a new slot costs 97,920 state gas and a changed slot 10,000 gas, so opening a position at two fresh ticks, which writes between 5 and 11 new slots, costs between about 0.4 and 1.0 million gas more than today, and a tick crossing, which changes two fee growth slots, about 14,000 more. A swap can still be split by its price limit and a removal touches a fixed number of slots. A native take to an address that does not exist would cost 183,600 state gas more. These are costs for the caller and no path becomes unreachable. I did not measure the deployed contract under the new rules.

cleared.check: Lead L-577: the arithmetic, comparison, shift, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, EXP, KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD, MLOAD, MSTORE, MCOPY, PUSH, DUP and SWAP implementations and their jump table entries at fork commit 0e44603, read against the specification.
cleared.result: Every entry maps the opcode to the matching function with the specified stack arity (core/vm/jump_table.go). Operand order follows the specification (instructions.go lines 34 to 235). SAR clamps above 256 and SRsh handles 256 itself, SHL and SHR clear at 256 or more, BYTE clears for an index of 32 or more including indexes above 2^64, SIGNEXTEND returns x for a byte index above 30, EXP of an even base by an exponent of 256 or more is zero, PUSH pads missing bytes with zeros on the right (lines 1166 to 1216). The PoolManager depends on these at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 and 48, src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:20-67, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:22 and 45 and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:219 and 252, and each gets the specified result.

cleared.check: Jump destination analysis and JUMP/JUMPI at fork commit 0e44603, and its cache.
cleared.result: codeBitmap marks the data bytes of PUSH1 to PUSH32 with the 8 and 16 byte helpers, which overwrite only bytes for positions not yet visited, and keeps 4 spare bytes for a trailing PUSH32 (core/vm/analysis_legacy.go lines 33 to 118). validJumpdest rejects targets at or past the code end and targets above 2^64, requires a JUMPDEST byte and a code segment (core/vm/contract.go lines 77 to 123). JUMPI tests the whole 256 bit word with IsZero (instructions.go lines 540 to 552). The cache is keyed by the code hash that resolveCodeHash returns, which for a delegated account is the hash of the code that resolveCode runs; the one mismatch, a delegation to a precompile under ArbOS 50 or later, runs no code (evm.go lines 791 to 821).

cleared.check: Lead L-577, CALL success flag, RETURNDATACOPY bounds and return data handling at fork commit 0e44603, against src/types/Currency.sol:64-74 and src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-148.
cleared.result: opCall pushes 1 or 0 after the child returns, then copies at most retSize bytes of the child output into memory only on success or revert, and sets the return data buffer to the full output (instructions.go lines 730 to 774). RETURNDATACOPY fails when offset plus length overflows or passes the buffer end (lines 312 to 328). Memory.Set copies the shorter of the two lengths (memory.go lines 52 to 64). The success test of Currency.transfer, which reads the word at 0 only when the return data is 32 bytes or more, and the return data copy of Hooks.callHook therefore see what they see on Ethereum.

cleared.check: Stack arena and pooled memory introduced in the fork interpreter: can a nested call, a Stylus program calling back into the EVM, or a pooled buffer change a value the PoolManager computed or the return data it reads.
cleared.result: The arena guarantees 1,024 free slots at the start of each frame and grows by reallocation (stack.go lines 55 to 70). Every opcode that runs a child frame pops its arguments by value before the call and pushes through the arena after it, so no pointer into the old backing array is written after a growth. Memory taken from the pool is zeroed up to its length on return and is never shrunk while in use, so a reused buffer exposes only zeros; buffers above 16 KiB are dropped (memory.go lines 25 to 49). Data handed to a child, to a LOG or returned by RETURN and REVERT is a copy or the caller memory that stays unchanged during the child. Stylus programs run through ExecuteWASM with the same arena (interpreter.go lines 168 to 172).

cleared.check: Part two, all instances. cleared.check: Whether the ruint 1.21.0 mul_mod fault described in OPCODES.md:120-136, which needs a modulus of four 64 bit limbs and a quotient of the product by the modulus within 2^129 of 2^256, can be reached by any MULMOD of this bytecode, for any input, on a node that runs that release.
cleared.result: No. Five MULMODs have the constant modulus 2^256-1 (four limbs), and the inputs of their callers bound the product: liquidity << 96 times a price difference or a price (2^384), a fee growth difference times liquidity (2^384), an amount times Q96 (2^352), an amount times a fee below 10^6, liquidity times a price difference (2^288). Their quotient is at most 2^128. Of the other eight, six have a modulus of at most three limbs: the constants 2^128, 2^96 and 10^6, liquidity (uint128), a sqrt price (uint160) and 10^6 minus the fee. The remaining two take n1 + product and n1 - product of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (SqrtPriceMath.sol:47 and 71), with a product n1 * sqrtPX96 below 2^384. A four limb modulus of at least 2^192 then leaves a quotient below 2^192. Both conditions of the fault never hold together in this code, whatever the input. This is stronger than the in-pool argument of OPCODES.md.

cleared.check: Part one. Which entries of the Solidity bug list apply to solc 0.8.26 with the settings of foundry.toml (via IR, optimizer on with 44,444,444 runs and the default Yul step sequence, Cancun), fetched again on 2026-11-24, and what SOL-2026-7 needs according to the primary source.
cleared.result: bugs_by_version.json lists eight entries for 0.8.26 (released 2024-05-21). By the conditions field of bugs.json six can apply to this build: SOL-2026-8 OverlappingRecursiveStorageStructCopyCorruptionViaIR (viaIR, introduced 0.8.13, fixed 0.8.39, needs a storage-to-storage copy of a recursive struct with a dynamic array into a target that contains the source), SOL-2026-7 YulOptimizerKnowledgeBaseStaleBookkeeping (yulOptimizer, 0.8.19 to 0.8.37, fixed 0.8.38, severity low), SOL-2026-6 MisorderedNamedParametersInRequireWithCustomErrors (viaIR, introduced 0.8.26, fixed 0.8.37, needs require(cond, Error({name: value})) ), SOL-2026-4 SpillSlotCollisionAcrossMutualRecursion (viaIR, fixed 0.8.37, needs a cycle of at least two mutually recursive functions), SOL-2026-2 UnsoundSpillInMutualRecursion (viaIR, fixed 0.8.36, needs intersecting recursive cycles) and SOL-2025-1 LostStorageArrayWriteOnSlotOverflow (no conditions, fixed 0.8.32, needs a storage array that crosses slot 2^256). Two cannot apply by their conditions: SOL-2026-8 for the evmasm pipeline (viaIR false) and SOL-2026-5 MemoryByteArrayElementDeleteClearsWholeWord (viaIR false). The post of 2026-10-22 confirms SOL-2026-7: affected steps LoadResolver (L) and EqualStoreEliminator (E), both in the default sequence; the trigger is a variable used to compute memory or storage addresses that is reassigned, one address derived from its value before and one after the reassignment with different constant offsets, and the two addresses equal at run time; then a load is replaced with an outdated value, a store of an equal value is removed, or a keccak256 is replaced. The fix is in 0.8.38 and is confined to KnowledgeBase and DataFlowAnalyzer. The default sequence in libsolidity/interface/OptimiserSettings.h at v0.8.26 contains three L and one E in the main part and none in the cleanup part fDnTOcmuO.

cleared.check: Does the installed solc 0.8.26 (solc-js 0.8.26+commit.8a97fa7a) carry SOL-2026-7, and what does its faulty output look like? The post's contract C was compiled three ways and run in tools/opdiff/pyevm.py with g(0, 2, 0xaaaa, 0xbbbb).
cleared.result: The via-IR build with the default sequence returns 0xaaaa; the via-IR build with every L and E removed and the evmasm build return 0xbbbb, which is what the source says. In the faulty irOptimized, sstore(var_i, calldataload(100)) with var_i reassigned in a loop is followed by return of the earlier calldata word instead of an sload. The compiler that built research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json therefore has the bug, and the shape to look for is a load replaced by a value across a store whose address uses a reassigned variable.

cleared.check: Parts two and three for SOL-2026-7 (leads L-028, L-151, L-152). Which L or E step of the default sequence acts on the PoolManager build, and does any load it replaces, or any store it removes, rely on an address whose base variable was reassigned?
cleared.result: Does not affect this build. A rebuild with the default sequence equals build/PoolManager.json in creation and runtime code. A rebuild with E and the first two L removed (sequence in pm.noL12E.json) also equals it byte for byte, so E removes no store and only the third L (in CTUca[r]LSs) shapes the output; without that L the build fails with stack too deep. The Yul of the Solidity pipeline was taken just before and just after that L (prefix sequences with an empty cleanup, no substitution of tload or tstore needed): the runtime loses 68 mload and 5 sload, no keccak256, tload or store changes (L3-loadcount.json). The 18 Yul functions where loads disappear were searched for variables assigned without let and for every mload, sload, mstore, sstore and keccak256 whose address uses such a variable or one derived from it (L3-reassign.json). In 17 of them no memory or storage address uses a reassigned variable, so the precondition of the bug is absent; this covers initialize, the five modifyLiquidity copies, beforeModifyLiquidity, updateTick (two sloads of the same TickInfo slot, Pool.sol:526-527), transferOwnership and onlyOwner (owner slot 0). In fun_swap 12 loads are replaced: 6 of params (a function argument, never reassigned), 2 of the step struct memPtr_1 (declared once, Pool.sol:340), and 4 of the named return result, which is assigned memPtr at the top and memPtr again only on the early return that leaves at once (Pool.sol:320). For all 12 there is no memory write and no call between the earlier load or store and the replaced load (L3-swap-replacements.json), so no aliasing decision of the KnowledgeBase was involved. The loads after the tick clamps (Pool.sol:351-356) stay. With nothing replaced across a store through a reassigned base, a compiler with the fix would make the same decisions on the same input.

cleared.check: Whether the optional switch dispatch interpreter of Bor v2.11.x, which a validator can enable with evm-switch-dispatch, computes a different result for any opcode the PoolManager uses.
cleared.result: No. The file was read in full. Every inlined opcode takes its operands in the jump table order and calls the same uint256 method, the stack checks are the same, JUMP and JUMPI check the jump destination before moving the program counter, and JUMPI tests the whole condition word. SAR with a shift of exactly 256 reaches SRsh, which returns zero for a non-negative value and all ones for a negative value, as specified. Constant gas of the inlined opcodes is charged before the next opcode that can have an effect, so the GAS opcode and every call see the same remaining gas. The setting is off by default.

cleared.check: The BNB Smart Chain rule that code cannot run at the block coinbase address (geth v1.8.2 core/vm/interpreter.go lines 96 to 98, reth-bsc src/evm/api/mod.rs lines 235 to 270): can an ordinary account use it against the PoolManager.
cleared.result: No. The coinbase is the signing address of the validator that produced the block, so only a validator can choose it, and it has code only if the validator delegated its own key through EIP-7702. A hook or token at that address would fail in that validator's blocks, which hurts only pools that chose such a contract. A native take to an address without code is not affected, because the rule applies only when code runs. Recorded with actor operator.

cleared.check: Whether an ordinary account can place a contract at an address that becomes a CAS20 precompile at Jenner, so that the code of a hook or currency changes after pools are created (A7).
cleared.result: Not feasible. The prefix rule fixes 0xca52 and eight zero bytes and limits byte 10 to two values, about 81 fixed bits, so a CREATE2 search for such an address needs about 2^80 hashes. Before Jenner these addresses hold no code, so sync and settle of such a currency revert in balanceOf and no account can be credited in it.

A take to the native asset addresses therefore reverts, and a take naming 0x100 as currency succeeds with empty data and debits the caller the full amount, as for any address without code. No call moves value that the caller does not owe.

cleared.check: Does the aarch64 build of Tempo compute DIV, MOD, MULMOD, ADDMOD, MUL, SHL and SAR the same as the x86-64 build, given that ruint 1.21.1 uses the x86-64 div instruction and _subborrow_u64 on x86-64 and the reciprocal and borrowing_sub fallback elsewhere.
cleared.result: Yes on 200 million cases. I built ruint 1.21.1 twice on x86-64, once unchanged and once with every target_arch = "x86_64" condition renamed so the fallback code compiles, and compared wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, mul_mod with a random and with the 2^256 - 1 modulus, add_mod, wrapping_mul, shift left and arithmetic shift right on operands built from zero, all ones, single bits, the top bit, near maximum limbs and shortened limb counts. No result differed, and the fallback quotient and remainder satisfied q*b + r = a with r < b in every case. This is the path FullMath.mulDiv and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp take on an ARM validator.

cleared.check: Does evm2 66687c18 have other code that depends on the CPU or build flags in the instruction paths the PoolManager uses.
cleared.result: Only data movement. write_word, write_u64 and to_usize_opt in utils.rs and swap_words in stack.rs have AVX, AVX2 or AVX-512 variants selected by compile time target features, which the release build does not set, and each variant as read stores or tests the same four limbs as the plain one. signextend, i256_div, i256_mod and i256_cmp are plain limb code. The 0xef configurable account instruction and the millisecond timestamp instruction that Tempo adds are absent from the PoolManager runtime as an opcode (a linear disassembly finds no 0x4f, 0xef or 0x1e opcode; the two 0x5e are MCOPY).

cleared.check: Does reuse of pooled interpreter frames in evm2 leak memory or return data from an earlier frame into a later one, which would change what the PoolManager reads with MLOAD, RETURNDATACOPY or the call input it borrows.
cleared.result: No. Interpreter::init clears memory, sets return data to empty, the stack length to zero and the output range to empty before a pooled frame runs, and memory grows through Vec::resize with zero fill. The main branch commit 8885390c only bounds the capacity idle frames keep.

cleared.check: Does any ruint fix between 1.20.0, which Arc runs, and 1.21.1 correct a result an EVM instruction uses.
cleared.result: No. 1.20.1 adds shifts by primitive integers. The 1.21.0 fix list names div_3x2_ref, which in 1.20.0 is exported and tested but never called by division (grep of src: definition in algorithms/div/small.rs and a test only). The mul_mod fault fixed in 1.21.1 was introduced in 1.21.0. 1.20.0 itself contains the overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr flag fix that also corrected byte().

On Arc: 194 seen, 186 checked, 994 ticks, 77,452 words, 106 comparisons, 0 violations. cleared.check: Part two (c), lead L-607: did the block producer roll back the transient unlock flag, the transient deltas and the pool storage of a PoolManager frame that reverted, in mined transactions where a later frame of the same transaction completed an unlock? The test compares, for each transaction, the receipt that the sequencer wrote with the status and surviving logs of debug_traceTransaction (callTracer, withLog) on the replica, which re-executes on the same pre-state.
cleared.result: Yes. 7,627 transactions emitted PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity logs between blocks 30,862,220 and 32,724,219. In 1,347 of them a frame that entered PoolManager.unlock reverted. In 1,333 of those the reverted frame contained a swap, the quoter pattern, and a later unlock in the same transaction completed. The receipt status and every surviving log equal the re-execution in all 7,627, with no trace errors. Had the producer kept the unlock flag (src/libraries/Lock.sol), the later unlock would revert with AlreadyUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:105). Had it kept the deltas (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol), the later unlock would fail with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Had it kept the reverted swap's slot0, the later Swap event would carry other prices. The window has no settle, take or sync inside a reverted frame.

cleared.check: Part three: whether a MegaETH per-frame budget (compute gas, data size, KV updates, state growth at 98/100 of the parent's remainder) or the detention cap after a volatile read can be breached in a child of the PoolManager's frame and caught there, so that the PoolManager continues with a failed subcall and returns another result than on Ethereum.
cleared.result: No. The resource limits spec says a child that exceeds its budget reverts with MegaLimitExceeded and the parent may continue. Every call the PoolManager makes treats failure as fatal: hooks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), native and ERC-20 transfers (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52, 73-86), balanceOf, a high-level call that reverts on failure (src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:285, 359), and unlockCallback (src/PoolManager.sol:110). The PoolManager reads gas() only to forward it. A breach below the PoolManager therefore reverts the PoolManager frame as a whole. A breach in the PoolManager's own frame reverts it as a whole for its caller. A transaction-level breach halts the transaction. The outcome is either the Ethereum result or a full revert, never a partial result. A token or hook that catches its own failed subcall is a token or hook matter and is not swept here.

cleared.check: Lead L-610: which per-frame budget a swap that crosses many initialized ticks reaches first, and whether a liquidity removal can reach one.
cleared.result: State growth binds first. Each crossing writes feeGrowthOutside0 and feeGrowthOutside1 of one tick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612). A write counts as state growth only when the slot was zero at transaction start (resource accounting, Storage Slot Growth Rules). Outside values are zero only for ticks initialized above the current tick (Pool.sol:533-538), so an upward swap through freshly planted ticks adds up to 2 per tick. The PoolManager frame at depth 1 gets 980 of the 1,000 per-transaction limit, so it reverts with MegaLimitExceeded after about 490 such ticks, at roughly 24 million compute gas from 2 cold loads, 2 fresh SSTOREs and a bitmap load per tick, inferred from standard gas costs and not measured. Ticks with nonzero outside values cost about 14,000 compute gas per crossing. 200 million compute gas then allows about 14,000 crossings, 28,000 KV updates and 1.1 MB of data size, far below the shares of 490,000 KV updates and 12.8 MB. The swapper can stop at a price limit and continue in a later transaction (Pool.sol:344), and each planted tick adds growth only on its first upward crossing. A removal touches two ticks and one position (Pool.sol:146-238). Cycle 1 recorded the same bound qualitatively. The result is a delay without loss, and an eth_call measurement through a router was not run.

cleared.check: Part four, lead L-601: is Rex6 active on MegaETH mainnet, and what does it change for the instruction set the PoolManager uses?
cleared.result: Active. The network upgrades overview gives Rex6 mainnet activation at timestamp 1787626800 (25 Aug 2026 03:00 UTC). mega-evm v1.7.3 scheduled it (#371), and the latest block read, 32,724,090, has timestamp 1795521101. Rex6 changes no opcode result. It sets one order for storage-gas and compute-gas charging (only CREATE2 changes), returns forwarded gas to the parent when a CALL or CREATE halts on the compute limit, adds a 32 byte data-size base per log, extends beneficiary detection to SELFDESTRUCT and EIP-7702 delegates, and corrects CREATE, EIP-7702, KeylessDeploy, fee-reward and system-transaction accounting. The PoolManager uses none of CREATE2, SELFDESTRUCT or KeylessDeploy. Its logs add 32 bytes each against a 13.1 MB limit. The forwarded-gas change affects gas_used only. The earlier 550-script pmdiff runs on MegaETH were made on 2026-11-24, after activation.

cleared.check: ruint advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0220, which affects every release before 1.20.0. mega-evm main pins ruint 1.19.0 and the stateless validator pins 1.17.2. In those releases wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr on 256 bit values truncate the shift amount modulo 2^32, and the overflowing and checked shift flags give false negatives.
cleared.result: Not reachable from the PoolManager's bytecode. revm v112 (interpreter 37.0.3) calls ruint's shift only when shift < 256 and returns zero or the sign fill otherwise, for SHL, SHR and SAR. BYTE calls byte() only for index < 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). The advisory says the shifted values were correct and only the flag was wrong, apart from the truncation above 2^32, which the guard excludes. The battery of OPCODES.md had already passed shift amounts at and above 256 on MegaETH.

cleared.check: Every MUL, MULMOD, ADDMOD and EXP of the 24,009 byte runtime, with the operands Monad v0.16.5's compiler sees as literals. The compiler tracks literals per basic block: a block that is a jump destination starts with no known values, and only a JUMPI whose fall-through block is not a jump destination keeps them. sites.py models that rule and the constant folding of pure opcodes.
cleared.result: There are 13 MULMOD and 85 MUL in the code. Two MULMOD have a literal power of two modulus in their block and so take the inline path mul_mod2: pc 22378 with 2^128 (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 in the copy of mulDiv called from src/libraries/Position.sol:94 and 96, PUSH17 at pc 22359) and pc 22639 with 2^96 (FullMath.sol:48 in the copy called from src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250, PUSH13 at pc 22624). The other eleven MULMOD go to the runtime call, which uses the 256 bit library shared with the interpreter: eight have no literal modulus or the modulus not(0) or 1000000 (pcs 22316, 22445, 22513, 22585, 22892, 22921, 23094, 23678), and three have the literal factor 2^96 with a modulus that is not(0) or unknown (pcs 20958, 22721, 22763). Twenty-five MUL have a literal operand: the first-step select of TickMath.sol:80 (pc 16780, literal 0x1fffcb933bd6fad37aa2d162d1a594001), the 19 multipliers of TickMath.sol:81-99 (pcs 17055 to 17557), the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 of TickMath.sol:225 (pc 18495), 3 times the denominator of FullMath.sol:82 (pcs 22777 and 22935), the BitMath.sol:34-47 constant (pc 21359) and the folded inverse of 15625 for the 1000000 denominator copy of FullMath.sol:99 (pc 22529). The first 23 have a zero 64 bit limb and are inlined through mul_with_bit_size; the last two have no zero limb and go to monad_vm_runtime_mul. The other 60 MUL multiply two values and go to monad_vm_runtime_mul. The EXP and ADDMOD bytes at pcs 24005 and 24008 are the metadata trailer. The deployed Monad PoolManager has the same bytes as the build except the 20 byte immutable at 13618-13637, so the pcs hold on chain.

cleared.check: MULMOD by 2^128 at pc 22378 and by 2^96 at pc 22639 as Monad v0.16.5 compiles them: modop_optimized (emitter.cpp 7590-7684) rewrites a power of two modulus into mul_mod2 (7991-8084), which for exp 96 and 128 (last_ix 1, inline_threshold 1) calls mul_with_bit_size(exp, a, b) with b in a general register or a stack slot (6720-6981), which runs MulEmitter (6465-6716) and mul_with_bit_size_by_rax (6381-6463). Transcribed instruction by instruction into Python (64 bit limbs, carry flag, 32 bit writes that clear the upper half, imul with a sign extended 32 bit immediate, mulx that leaves flags alone, rdx saved through a spare register, through rbx or on the machine stack) and run against Python integers.
cleared.result: No mismatch in 1,000,000 cases for each modulus. The operands were random, all limbs set, 2^256-1, low one or two limbs zero, one below 2^128 and the other above, powers of two, negative values and limb patterns of 0, 1, 2^31, 2^32, 2^63 and 2^64-1. The left operand started in a general register, a stack slot or a vector register, the right in a register or a stack slot, 15 percent with both in the same slot, with random choices of which of the three register sets hold other live values. Every rdx branch of mul_with_bit_size ran (dst holds rdx, swapped with tmp, through a spare register or rbx; left holds rdx; rdx live on the stack, pushed or moved). For 96 bits no mask is applied (96 & 31 is 0), and the top limb is right because every operation on it is a 32 bit one; a mutation that keeps the upper half on 32 bit writes fails all 4,000 of 4,000 cases, and mutations that drop the high half of mulx fail more than half, so the harness sees such faults. The remainder these sites return equals mulmod(a, b, 2^exp) for every input tried, so the reconstructed quotient of the two mulDiv copies is the specified one.

cleared.check: MUL with one literal operand as mul_optimized (emitter.cpp 6983-7043) compiles it: power of two or negated power of two literals to a shift, literals with a zero limb to mul_with_bit_size(256), other literals to the runtime call. Run for the 24 literals the PoolManager multiplies by (the 19 TickMath multipliers, the first-step select whose third limb is 1 and so takes the copy shortcut of mul_sequence, 255738958999603826347141 times a signed log_2, 3, and the two full width constants), and for random literals.
cleared.result: No mismatch in 1,000,000 cases over the 24 site literals (916,672 inline, 83,328 runtime) and 1,000,000 cases with random literals (724,402 inline, 128,504 runtime, 116,601 shift). The multiplicands included negative two's complement values, which is what getTickAtSqrtPrice feeds the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 for prices below 1. The 32 bit immediate form is used only for limbs inside the signed 32 bit range (is_uint64_bounded<int32_t>, emitter.cpp 243-258 with the default in emitter.hpp); a mutation that allows the unsigned range fails 2,741 of 4,000 random literal cases.

cleared.check: monad_vm_runtime_mul and monad_vm_runtime_mul_192 of runtime/math.S, which every compiled MUL of two variables uses (a*b of FullMath.sol:21, prod1*twos of FullMath.sol:75, the six inverse steps of FullMath.sol:86-91, result = prod0*inv of FullMath.sol:99, r*r of TickMath.sol:142-221), transcribed instruction by instruction, with the result pointer equal to either operand and with both operand pointers equal.
cleared.result: No mismatch in 1,000,000 cases for each of the two routines, and r12 and r13 are restored. The routines read every limb they need from an operand before they write the first result limb that can share its address, which is the overlap rule intrinsics.hpp states. math.S is identical at v0.16.5, v0.16.6 and v0.16.7.

cleared.check: Every tick of the range through the compiled multiplication paths: getSqrtPriceAtTick (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:59-114) and getTickAtSqrtPrice of its result (TickMath.sol:123-236), with each MUL replaced by the transcription of the path it compiles to, a fresh random register picture for each product, and mul(r, r) through monad_vm_runtime_mul with both pointers equal.

cleared.check: Correction to the cycle 9 note on mined coverage of the compiled MULMOD by 2^96. The 183 Monad swaps of opcodes/monad-rounding.json carry the rounding bit of SqrtPriceMath.sol:252, which is the MULMOD at pc 23094.

The mined swaps therefore test the shared library, which earlier cycles also tested through simulated calls, and say nothing about pc 22378 or 22639. cleared.check: Which mined Monad results exercise each compiled path, from 1,580 Swap events of 31 pools in blocks 124,993,964 to 124,996,219 read with eth_getLogs.
cleared.result: The TickMath literal multiplies and the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 run on every swap, and bits 0x1 to 0x40000 of the absolute tick all appear in the emitted ticks (0x20000 in 844 swaps, 0x40000 in 463), while 0x80000 appears in none. The general mulDiv 512 bit branch, with the multiply by 3 at pc 22935 and the runtime inverse products, is reachable in these pools: 751 consecutive pairs have (liquidity << 96) times the price at or above 2^256. pc 22639 needs liquidity times the price step at or above 2^256; the largest liquidity seen has 74 bits and the largest product 159 bits, so no mined swap in the window ran it. pc 22378 runs only in Position.update when the fee growth difference times the liquidity reaches 2^256, and ModifyLiquidity events do not carry amounts, so no mined result shows it. The way to confirm either site from blocks without sending a transaction is to find a mined swap or liquidity change whose inputs cross that bound and compare the token amounts of its Swap event or of the token Transfer events with the formulas; none was found in the window.

cleared.check: Whether an ordinary account can steer a victim pool into the two inline MULMOD sites, which would matter if they were wrong.

This is the operator's validator agreeing with the operator's node. The rollup has one whitelisted validator, the EOA 0x8e87f7c65750c25c6708de33823124cf457676b2, which sent the confirming transactions itself, and the whitelist is enabled. It is not an independent replay, so the unnamed vlocal+unknown go1.25.12 build rests on the opcode battery and the PoolManager scripts run against the endpoint. Robinhood Chain is in the same position with two whitelisted validators.

cleared.check: Is the consensus path exposed to Go issue 81863, the dead store miscompile of go1.26.0 to go1.26.10 and go1.27.0 to go1.27.3?
cleared.result: No. The WAVM machine that defines the settled state is built with go1.25.9 at both v3.12.4 and the consensus-v61 tag, and the bad compiler commit landed after the go1.25 branch, as cycle 9 recorded. Only the native nodes carry it, which F-117 already covers.

cleared.check: Has holiman/uint256 or upstream go-ethereum moved to new arithmetic code that these chains might pick up with v3.13.0?
cleared.result: There is no release after v1.3.2, and go-ethereum master and v1.17.4 to v1.17.6 still pin v1.3.2. The unreleased master of uint256 rewrites Div and Mod and adds a shift path for power-of-two divisors (the FullMath.sol:62, 67, 73 shape). A transcription of that code matched Python integers on 298,076 general cases and 21,792 FullMath and TickMath.sol:104 shaped cases. It needs a fresh test whenever a release pins it. Two planted faults were caught: one wrong bit in the two-limb quotient gave 2,517 mismatches in 19,873 cases, and an off-by-one shift in the power-of-two path gave 148 (raw/uint256_master_planted.txt).

cleared.check: RUSTSEC-2026-0220 on X Layer, which pins ruint 1.18.0: can a SHL, SHR, SAR or BYTE amount of 2^32 or more, or a non limb aligned overflow flag, give a wrong result to TickBitmap, BitMath or the BalanceDelta and Slot0 unpacking.
cleared.result: No. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (crates.io, the version X Layer pins) converts the amount with as_usize_saturated and calls the ruint shift only when it is below 256, returning zero or the sign fill otherwise; BYTE calls byte() only for an index below 32 (instructions/bitwise.rs lines 107-158). The advisory states the shifted values were correct and only the flags were wrong apart from the truncation above 2^32, which the guard excludes. ruint 1.18.0 byte() indexes the little endian limb slice directly (bits.rs lines 71-82). 3,045 new vectors with amounts k*2^32 + r, 2^64 + r, 2^128 + r and 2^255 + r for SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE and SIGNEXTEND on seven values, each sent three times, gave 0 mismatches on both networks.

cleared.check: Can the CIP-64 fee debit or credit on celo-kona main leave transient storage that a later frame of the user's transaction reads at the PoolManager (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36).
cleared.result: No. The debit's transient storage is cleared after the debit commits and before the main call (handler.rs around line 698). cleared.check: Can an ordinary account use the X Layer gasless rule against PoolManager users.
cleared.result: No. A transaction is gasless only if the whitelist contract allows its target and calldata, and none of the PoolManager, PositionManager or Universal Router targets is allowed. The rule skips fees only; the PoolManager bytecode reads neither GASPRICE nor BASEFEE (OPCODES.md, bytecode level), and BASEFEE keeps the header value.

cleared.check: Part one: is the public MegaETH stateless validator run by any party that publishes its results or mismatches?
cleared.result: No public publisher was found. The documentation describes the validator, a fatal stop on any header commitment mismatch, and an optional --report-validation-endpoint that sends mega_setValidatedBlocks callbacks to an operator-chosen endpoint, but names no public operator or feed. L2BEAT lists state validation as fraud proofs with fewer than five external challengers. The validator was not run in this unit (no software built), so the producer's storage writes are covered by the replica's re-execution and eth_getStorageAt only, as above.

cleared.check: Part two, lead L-627: do nanoreth and hyper-evm-sync compare state root and receipts root with what hl-node produced, and do they stop on a mismatch?
cleared.result: Receipts yes, state no. nanoreth (commit f0cad31, the build at rpc.purroofgroup.com) checks gas used, receipts root and logs bloom after execution and returns an InsertBlockError on a mismatch, which leaves the block invalid and the node unable to advance. Its reth fork replaces the computed state root with zero before comparing it with the header, whose stateRoot is zero. hyper-evm-sync asserts receipts (success, cumulative gas, logs) and panics on a mismatch; its blake3 state hash is not compared. Both inject the results of HyperCore read precompiles from the block files. Both clients also carry the same 18 hard-coded state patches for improper self destructs in blocks 1,467,569 to 1,531,366, which shows that the validator once wrote state that stock revm would not; all are before the PoolManager's first log after block 45,998,366, and the PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT. Recorded as an operator level information finding.

cleared.check: Part three: in bor v2.11.1, are transient storage and the access list per transaction under BlockSTM, and does a re-executed incarnation start clean?
cleared.result: Yes. Each incarnation builds its state from a fresh copy of the clean state (core/parallel_state_processor.go:127-138, setupEVM, cleanStateDB.Copy()). ApplyMessage reaches StateTransition, which calls Prepare (core/state_transition.go:561); Prepare creates a new access list (core/state/statedb.go:3023-3026) and a new transient storage map (statedb.go:3050-3051). Transient writes are journaled (statedb.go:1370-1376) and reverted with the frame (core/state/journal.go:419-421). Transient storage is not part of the multi-version write set: MVWriteList omits reverted keys (statedb.go:295-305) and ApplyMVWriteSet copies the incarnation's current value of each persistent path (statedb.go:693-702), so a storage write undone by a reverted frame is settled at its restored value.

cleared.check: Do reth v2.11.0 (Ethereum endpoint), op-reth v2.8.1 (OP Mainnet) and op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1 (Unichain, Ink, Soneium) put the alloy-primitives keccak cache in front of KECCAK256, and with which versions.
cleared.result: Yes for all three, by default, with the same text cycle 10 read for Tempo. reth bin/reth/Cargo.toml lines 88-99 list keccak-cache-global in default and lines 135-139 forward it to alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global. op-reth rust/op-reth/bin/Cargo.toml line 38 lists it in default and lines 68-72 forward it through reth-optimism-cli and reth-optimism-node, whose own feature (op-reth/crates/cli/Cargo.toml lines 82-85, crates/node/Cargo.toml lines 129-132) sets alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global. The three lockfiles pin alloy-primitives 1.7.3 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (reth Cargo.lock line 4365, op-reth v2.8.1 line 5259, v2.9.0-rc.1 line 5260). The endpoints answered web3_clientVersion with reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc, op-reth/v2.8.1-72207294 (and an unversioned op-reth dev build on OP Mainnet) and op-reth/v2.9.0-rc.1-72fcf947. No mismatch appeared in the bucket test of this cycle on any of the five.

cleared.check: Does Base v1.5.6 enable the keccak cache, through which edge, and is its alloy-primitives version a text not yet read.
cleared.result: It is enabled by default. bin/node/Cargo.toml line 31 lists keccak-cache-global in default and line 33 forwards it to base-execution-cli, whose feature (crates/execution/cli/Cargo.toml lines 113-115) sets base-node-core and reth-node-core (base/reth tag base-v2.5.2.11, crates/node/core/Cargo.toml line 5: alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global). The lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.1 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (Cargo.lock line 9776). The keccak_cache.rs of the 1.6.1 crate is byte identical to that of 1.7.3 (diff of the two crates from static.crates.io printed nothing), so the cache text is the one already read: a OnceLock holding fixed_cache::Cache::new(1 << 17), EPOCHS false, STATS only with keccak-cache-stats, which no Base manifest read sets. The endpoint reported reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/.../base/v1.5.6, and the bucket test found no mismatch.

cleared.check: Does X Layer (xlayer-reth v0.0.7) enable the keccak cache, and does its combination of alloy-primitives 1.6.0 with fixed-cache 0.1.10, which neither Tempo nor Arc runs, behave as the read versions do.
cleared.result: It is enabled, although bin/node/Cargo.toml line 75 has default = [] and its own asm-keccak feature does not touch the cache. The edge is the reth crate: bin/node/Cargo.toml line 28 takes reth.workspace, the workspace Cargo.toml line 89 pins reth from okx/reth rev 81573d2c without default-features = false, and that crate's bin/reth/Cargo.toml lists keccak-cache-global in default (lines 85-91) and forwards it to alloy-primitives/keccak-cache-global (lines 119-122). The lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.0 and fixed-cache 0.1.10 (Cargo.lock line 3767). The keccak_cache.rs of 1.6.0 is byte identical to that of 1.5.7 (Arc's text): a static cache built by fixed_cache::static_cache! with COUNT 1 << 17 (line 13), EPOCHS false (line 20), inputs of 0 bytes or more than 87 bytes skip the cache (lines 23-26). In fixed-cache 0.1.10 the static_cache! macro builds every bucket with Bucket::new(), which sets tag 0 and zeroed data (lib.rs line 583-585), so the first lookup of any bucket sees a key of length 0 that never equals a nonempty input. The get and insert paths are those of the next item. The endpoint reported reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/.../xlayer/v0.0.7, and the bucket test found no mismatch.

cleared.check: Reread of the fixed-cache 0.1.10 get and insert paths that every cache user in this list runs: key equality, lock protocol, epochs, and what a reader sees while a writer is inserting.
cleared.result: No path returns a hash for another input. calc (lib.rs lines 527-540) takes bucket = hash & (capacity - 1) and tag = hash & !(capacity - 1). Key and value are Copy types, so NEEDS_DROP is false and ALIVE_BIT is never set, and EPOCHS is false in both alloy texts, so the epoch bits are not used. The tag never has bit 0 set because the low 17 bits are masked off. get_inner (lines 322-350) succeeds only if a Relaxed load of the bucket state equals the tag exactly and a compare-exchange from tag to tag | LOCKED_BIT with Acquire succeeds (try_lock_ret, lines 593-606). While a writer holds the bucket the state carries LOCKED_BIT, so a reader's expected value does not match and it returns None and hashes the input itself. Under the lock the reader returns the stored value only if key.equivalent holds, which for [u8] against Key compares the slice of length len, so length and every byte must match (alloy keccak_cache.rs line 88 in 1.6.0, line 128 in 1.6.1). insert_inner (lines 389-439) takes the lock with expected None, which fails if the bucket is locked, writes key and value together, and releases with a Release store of the new tag (unlock, line 613). An ABA case in which another key with the same 64 bit hash replaces the entry between the reader's load and its compare-exchange leaves a reader that fails the equality test and recomputes. The value stored is imp(input) computed for the same input as the key (get_or_try_insert_with_ref, lines 506-524). This build has no lock-free read path: the string LOCK_FREE does not occur in lib.rs.

cleared.check: Does the KECCAK256 opcode go through the cache in each interpreter these nodes run, and does the hashing of storage keys for the state trie go through it as well.
cleared.result: Both do where the feature is on, and only the opcode result reaches the PoolManager. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer), 42.0.0 (Base) and 43.0.2 (op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1) implement KECCAK256 in instructions/system.rs lines 18-40 as KECCAK_EMPTY for length 0, else primitives::keccak256 over the memory slice, and revm-primitives 24.0.1, 42.0.0 and 43.0.0 re-export alloy_primitives::keccak256 (lib.rs lines 39-41). evm2 at rev 66687c18, which reth v2.11.0 runs, calls alloy_primitives::keccak256 in interpreter/instructions/crypto.rs lines 2 and 14. alloy-primitives utils/mod.rs lines 147-150 route keccak256 through keccak_cache::compute when keccak-cache-global is set. reth's trie hashes account and slot keys with the same function (crates/trie/common/src/key.rs line 16, hashed_state.rs line 55). Those hashed keys feed the state root. SLOAD and SSTORE look up the plain slot word, so a wrong trie key hash would give a wrong state root and a halted or forked node, while the slot the PoolManager reads and writes comes only from the KECCAK256 opcode result.

cleared.check: Bucket collision test: KECCAK256 of 1 to 88 byte inputs chosen to share a bucket of the cache, sent interleaved so each lookup evicts the previous entry, in parallel requests, against the Python keccak.
cleared.result: No wrong hash on any of the 14 endpoints. The bucket index is hash & (2^17 - 1) with hash = rapidhash_v3_micro_inline::<false, false>(input, RapidSecrets::seed(0)) (alloy keccak_cache.rs lines 48-60 in 1.6.0, 88-100 in 1.6.1; fixed-cache calc; rapidhash 4.4.1 and 4.5.1 v3/rapid_const.rs lines 236-310, which are identical in the two versions). The script transcribes that function in Python. A pool of 34,400 inputs (300 random inputs of each length 1 to 88, 3,000 delta-slot inputs of address word then currency word as CurrencyDelta.sol builds them, 2,000 mapping-slot inputs and 3,000 position-key inputs of 58 bytes as Position.sol builds them) fell into 3,723 buckets that hold two or more inputs. 3,528 of those buckets mix lengths and 1,556 hold a PoolManager-shaped input. Each bucket was sent as A B A B A B plus A without its last byte, A with an extra zero byte and A again. 300 extra groups put 87 byte inputs, which are cached, next to their 88 byte extensions, which skip the cache. That is 36,059 hashes per round, in chunks of 500 records, four requests at a time, three rounds per endpoint, 108,177 hashes per endpoint, all as specified. World Chain and Celo do not enable the cache by their manifests and served as controls. Polygon's eth_call does not reach Bor's block-import cache (next item). The transcription of rapidhash could not be compared with the compiled crate because building a Rust harness was not permitted in this session. If it is wrong, the inputs still exercise the cache at random buckets, and every result was checked.

cleared.check: Do World Chain v2.8.2 and Celo's celo-reth enable keccak-cache-global.
cleared.result: Neither does, as far as the manifests read show. World Chain: bin/world-chain/Cargo.toml line 40 has default = ["jemalloc"], the workspace takes reth-node-core, reth-cli-util and all reth-optimism crates with default-features = false (Cargo.toml lines 132, 177, 185-197), and the Dockerfile builds with FEATURES="jemalloc" (line 37). Its lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.1 and fixed-cache 0.1.10, so if the cache were turned on it would run the text already read. Celo: forno answered with reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb, which matches the reth-node-core patch to celo-org/reth rev 74cc8bbc in celo-kona tag celo/reth-v1.0.10 (Cargo.toml line 466). The celo-reth crate (crates/celo-reth/Cargo.toml line 146) has default = ["std"] and no cache feature, its Dockerfile builds -p celo-reth with no features, and the patched reth-optimism-node at celo-org/optimism b08a8d0 has default = ["reth-codec"] (line 110). Its lockfile pins alloy-primitives 1.6.0 with fixed-cache 0.1.8, the versions read for Arc. In one of three requests forno answered from a different backend, Geth/v0.1.0-untagged-c7ed55b8-20260817 (go1.24.13), which is a geth-family node with no alloy cache. No full cargo feature resolution was run, so a feature set by a crate outside those read cannot be excluded. The bucket test matched on both.

cleared.check: Does the public MegaETH stateless validator compile the keccak cache.
cleared.result: No. Its Cargo.lock (megaeth-labs/stateless-validator, main branch as fetched on 2026-11-24, version 2.1.0, mega-evm tag v1.7.3, revm 40.0.3, ruint 1.17.2) contains no fixed-cache package, and the alloy-primitives 1.6.0 entry does not list it as a dependency, so keccak-cache-global cannot be on in any build of that lock. The RPC node, mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc, is not public, and the bucket test on it found no mismatch.

cleared.check: Bor v2.11.1, which the Polygon publicnode endpoint reports (bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private), adds its own cache of 64 byte KECCAK256 results. Can it return a hash for another input.
cleared.result: No. opKeccak256 (core/vm/instructions.go lines 259-290) uses the cache only when the input is exactly 64 bytes and evm.Config.Keccak256Cache is set. It copies all 64 bytes into a [64]byte key, and on a miss it hashes the data and stores (key, hash). Keccak256Cache is BoundedCache[[64]byte, common.Hash] (keccak_cache.go line 26), a sync.Map keyed by the whole array, written with LoadOrStore so an entry is never replaced, and capped at 65,536 entries, past which Store does nothing (bounded_cache.go lines 28-59). The cache is created per block in ProcessBlock (blockchain.go lines 1276-1288, 1328-1329 and 1348) and given to the prefetcher and the BlockSTM V2 workers. Speculative runs can only add pairs of an input and its true hash, which are right in any later run. eth_call does not set the field, so the bucket test on Polygon could not reach it. The 64 byte inputs it serves are the delta slots and mapping slots of src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-14 and src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:69-70. The same block adds an ecrecover result cache (core/vm/evm.go lines 57-87). The PoolManager source has no ecrecover or staticcall (grep of src/), so that cache is outside its path.

cleared.check: Do the other geth-family clients put a cache in front of KECCAK256.
cleared.result: Not in the sources read. BSC v1.8.2 (the version the BSC endpoint reports) computes crypto.Keccak256Hash(data) on every call (core/vm/instructions.go lines 232-243). The OffchainLabs go-ethereum master branch, which Nitro builds on, and the ava-labs libevm main branch, which avalanchego 1.15.3 builds on, reset a per-interpreter Keccak state and hash the data on every call (instructions.go lines 236-246 in both). For Nitro and libevm these are branch heads, not the commits the endpoints run.

cleared.check: L-633: X Layer pins ruint 1.18.0 and Base ruint 1.19.0, inside RUSTSEC-2026-0220. Does every SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE handler of the revm-interpreter they pin clamp the amount before calling ruint, and does any precompile or handler they run call a ruint shift with an unclamped amount.
cleared.result: The handlers clamp, and the other code read has no unclamped shift. The advisory says the shifted values of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr were right and only the overflow flag was wrong, and that wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr took the amount modulo 2^32. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer) and 42.0.0 (Base) convert the amount with as_usize_saturated (macros.rs lines 122-126) and call << and >> (which are wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr) and arithmetic_shr only when the amount is below 256, else return 0 or the sign fill. BYTE indexes only below 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). SIGNEXTEND shifts by at most 247 (arithmetic.rs lines 126-136). A Python transcription of the ruint 1.19.0 u256 paths of wrapping_shl, wrapping_shr and arithmetic_shr (bits.rs lines 437-467, 573-603, 612-623) matched the EVM definition on 509,184 cases covering every amount 0 to 255. A grep of revm-precompile 36.0.3 and 42.0.1, op-revm 20.0.0, revm-handler 20.0.3 and 42.0.1, alloy-evm 0.36.0 and 0.38.0 and alloy-op-evm 0.32.0 finds no call to a wrapping, overflowing, checked or saturating shift, and every << or >> with a U256 operand uses a constant amount. Base's crates/common/evm sources (precompiles/mod.rs, handler.rs, evm.rs and the other 11 files) shift only by constants. base-common-evm2 is in the Base workspace, but no package in the Base lockfile depends on it. The xlayer-reth crates directory has no EVM or precompile crate (builder, chainspec, flashblocks, intercept, legacy-rpc, monitor, rcs-filter, rpc, tests, version), and those crates were not read line by line.

cleared.check: Which of the settlement opcodes Monad v0.16.5 compiles inline and which it hands to a runtime function that the interpreter also calls, and how the compiled code passes operands and takes the result of such a call.
cleared.result: Inline in compiled code: CALLER and ADDRESS (read_context_address), CALLVALUE (read_context_word), RETURNDATASIZE, CALLDATASIZE and MSIZE (read_context_uint32_to_word), CALLDATALOAD (Emitter::calldataload with the assembly helper monad_vm_runtime_load_bounded_le_raw) and SIGNEXTEND. Handed to a runtime function: KECCAK256 (runtime::sha3), CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE, CALL, STATICCALL and SELFBALANCE (emitter.hpp 388-485, 525-552). The interpreter's instruction table calls the same runtime functions for these (instruction_table.hpp 821-833, 942-954, 1053-1065, 1306-1318, 1360-1390), so the eth_call tests of earlier cycles (the KECCAK256, MCOPY and copy vectors of the battery and the 50 call semantics tests of callsem.py) ran the code that block execution runs for them. The only compiled-specific part is the call glue. RuntimeImpl::pass stores every operand that is in a register into its stack slot, call_impl passes each operand as a pointer to that slot or to a rodata copy of a literal, in pop order, which is the order of the C++ parameters for every function above, and the result is written to a fresh stack slot at the new top (emitter.cpp 443-501). That slot can be the slot of the deepest input, which is the same aliasing the interpreter uses (call_runtime.hpp: the result pointer is the deepest stack argument). Each of these functions reads all its inputs before it writes the result: sha3 reads size and offset first (keccak.hpp 28-45), tload copies the key first (storage.hpp 35-45), and call and staticcall take the operands by reference into call_impl and write the result after it returns (call.cpp 198-221, 272-293). CALLVALUE uses the 32 byte big-endian env.value through movbe per limb or vpermq plus vpshufb, both a full byte reversal.

cleared.check: Monad v0.16.5 inline CALLDATALOAD at every offset location the emitter distinguishes (literal up to 2^31-1, literal from 2^31 to 2^32-1 through rodata, literal of 2^32 or more, general register live and not live in each of the three register sets, AVX register, stack slot), with is_bounded_by_bits<32>, the 32 byte load or the bounded load helper for fewer than 32 remaining bytes, and the byte swap.
cleared.result: No mismatch with the specification in 411,200 cases: every calldata length from 0 to 300 with every offset from 0 to length plus 40 and nine large offsets at each location, and 50,000 random cases with lengths up to 5,000 and offsets whose upper limbs are set. Every branch of monad_vm_runtime_load_bounded_le_raw ran (sizes 1, 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 8, 9 to 16, 17 to 31 and zero or negative), and no case read a byte outside the calldata buffer. The 17 to 24 byte case depends on shrd and shrx masking a count of 64 to 120 to six bits; the transcription models that masking and the result is right. Seven of ten planted faults were caught (between 280 and 31,960 failing cases each); the three not caught are equivalent for calldata below 2^31 bytes (a 16 bit size read, a 31 bit offset mask and the rodata threshold). The PoolManager runs CALLDATALOAD at 44 sites, 40 with a literal offset; in the 584 scripts compared below the compiled transcription executed it 84,050 times in the PoolManager.

cleared.check: Monad v0.16.5 inline CALLER, CALLVALUE and RETURNDATASIZE, which decide who is credited (src/PoolManager.sol:301, 306, 369), how much native currency a settle credits (src/PoolManager.sol:354) and whether a token transfer counts as successful (src/types/Currency.sol:68).
cleared.result: No mismatch. CALLER: 50,000 addresses including all limb edges give the 160 bit value, with the top limb zero and the 32 bit movbe clearing the upper half of its register. CALLVALUE: 100,000 values through both the general register and the AVX destination. RETURNDATASIZE: every size from 0 to 4,096 and 5,000 random sizes below 2^24. RETURNDATASIZE reads the low 32 bits of a 64 bit field (static_assert at emitter.cpp 3072-3074); this is exact for return data below 2^32 bytes, which a transaction cannot produce under Monad's memory limit. When a comparison is held in the CPU flags, the three readers write zero with mov instead of xor, so the flags that Currency.transfer's gt(returndatasize(), 31) and eq(mload(0), 1) feed into are kept.

cleared.check: Monad v0.16.5 SIGNEXTEND with a non-literal index: destructive_mov_stack_elem_to_bounded_rax at its three index locations (general register live and not live, AVX, stack slot with and without a free register) and the three value paths signextend_avx_reg_by_bounded_rax, signextend_general_reg_by_bounded_rax and signextend_stack_offset_or_literal_by_bounded_rax.

cleared.check: How compiled CALL and STATICCALL return into the caller on Monad v0.16.5: the return data buffer, the caller's memory and the transient storage journal when the callee reverts, and whether a revert inside compiled code undoes TSTORE through the same journal as the interpreter.
cleared.result: Both paths run runtime::call_impl. It clears the return data before the call, stores the callee's output as the new return data after host->call, copies min(retSize, output size) into the caller's memory whatever the status, and pushes 1 only for EVMC_SUCCESS (call.cpp 58-196). The journal sits outside the VM: execute_call_message runs pre_call, which pushes a State version, then VM::execute on either path, then post_call, which accepts the version on success and rejects it otherwise (execute_message.cpp 110-174, 305-350). Transient storage lives in the versioned account state (state.cpp 126-180, 318-330, 406-410), so a revert in compiled code is undone exactly as in the interpreter. VM::execute_raw picks interpreted or native code inside that bracket (vm.cpp 142-190), and both end in rt_ctx.copy_to_evmc_result (vm.cpp 232-256). This repeats the cycle 4 and cycle 8 readings, which were taken from the main branch, on the v0.16.5 tag.

cleared.check: Lead L-623, first half: does debug_traceTransaction with callTracer on Monad execute the transaction again, or return the frames that block execution recorded?
cleared.result: It returns recorded frames. In monad-rpc, debug_traceTransaction replays only for prestateTracer (requires_replay matches Tracer::PreStateTracer only); for callTracer it calls monad_debug_traceTransaction, which reads the RLP call frames stored for the transaction (get_transaction_call_frame) and decodes them. Block execution writes those frames to the database through CommitBuilder::add_call_frames. The executor behind eth_call and debug_traceCall builds its VM as InterpreterOnly. So a recorded trace shows what the block, with the PoolManager compiled once hot, computed, and debug_traceCall shows what the interpreter computes. The monad-rpc reading is from the master branch of monad-bft; which commit rpc.monad.xyz runs was not confirmed (web3_clientVersion returns Monad/unknown).

cleared.check: Recorded block execution against interpreter replay for the first user transaction of a block (index 1; index 0 of every Monad block is the staking system call to 0x...1000) in 2,400 mined PoolManager transactions of blocks 124,987,459 to 125,011,397. Each was replayed with debug_traceCall at the parent block with its sender, target, input, value, gas and access list.
cleared.result: No difference that the PoolManager produced. The 2,400 trees hold 287,515 frames and 28,811 PoolManager frames: 5,369 unlock, 5,690 swap, 4,778 sync, 5,468 settle, 5,926 take, 1 mint. 1,078 transactions replay with an identical event sequence (every call, input, value, output, error and log in execution order), covering 6,017 PoolManager frames. In the other 1,322 the first differing event never belongs to the PoolManager. It is the staking precompile's answer (846), a bot contract that logs the block number (286), or a contract whose behaviour depends on the block (190). Pairing PoolManager frames by position and input gives 22,930 pairs, and 22,893 have identical outputs, errors, logs and outgoing calls. The other 37 come after an earlier divergence elsewhere in the same transaction: a token's balanceOf returned another balance, so settle returned another amount. 285 transactions hold a reverted frame that had entered unlock, followed by an unlock that completed. In 282 of them every PoolManager pair is identical. The first comparison without access lists gave false differences: the replay ran out of gas where the block had warm slots. Passing the access list removed every PoolManager-owned divergence.

cleared.check: Across the other networks: does block execution run the settlement opcodes on a code path that a simulated call does not reach?
cleared.result: No for these 18. Their blocks and their eth_call run the same interpreter: go-ethereum and its forks (BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Avalanche, the three Nitro chains), revm on the OP Stack and Arc, and evm2 on Ethereum's reth nodes and Tempo, whose published binaries have no compiler. The opcode battery, the call semantics tests and the script sets therefore test the block path there. MegaETH (4326) runs a closed compiling executor; cycle 10 compared 7,627 receipts, including 1,333 with a reverted unlock frame (F-118). HyperEVM's validator (999) is closed and stays an open gap. Monad (143) is covered by the entries above.
